title.zh: 卷73 列傳第38 循吏
title.raw: 卷73 列傳第38 循吏 Volume 73 Biographies 38: Upright Officials

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 循吏古之善牧人者，養之以仁，使之以義，教之以禮，隨其所便而處之，因其所欲而與之，從其所好而勸之。

translations.literal: Upright officials were of old those skilled at tending the people; they nourished them with benevolence, employed them through righteousness, instructed them with ritual, accommodated them according to what was convenient, granted them according to what they desired, and encouraged them by following what they preferred.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, an upright official was someone who truly knew how to shepherd the people: he nurtured them with benevolence, directed them through duty, taught them proper conduct, placed them where circumstances suited them best, gave them what they sought, and encouraged them by appealing to what they valued.

sentences.zh: 如父母之愛子，如兄之愛弟，聞其饑寒為之哀，見其勞苦為之悲，故人敬而悅之，愛而親之。

translations.literal: Like parents loving their children, like elder brothers loving younger brothers—they grieved on hearing of their hunger and cold, sorrowed on seeing their toil and hardship; thus the people respected and delighted in them, loved and drew near to them.
translations.idiomatic: They cared for the people as parents love their children or as an elder brother loves a younger one: hearing of hunger and cold, they felt sorrow; seeing toil and hardship, they were moved to grief. For this reason the people held them in respect and affection and drew close to them willingly.

sentences.zh: 若子產之理鄭國，子賤之居單父，賈琮之牧冀州，文翁之為蜀郡，皆可以恤其災患，導以忠厚，因而利之，惠而不費。

translations.literal: Such men as Zichan in governing the state of Zheng, Zijian in residing at Danfu, Jia Cong in pasturing Jizhou, and Wen Weng in administering Shu commandery—were all able to relieve the people's disasters and distress, lead them with sincerity and generosity, thereby benefit them, and show favor without expense.
translations.idiomatic: Figures such as Zichan governing Zheng, Zijian at Danfu, Jia Cong as inspector of Jizhou, and Wen Weng as magistrate of Shu—all comforted their people in times of disaster, guided them with sincere goodwill, turned that goodwill to practical benefit, and bestowed kindness at no ruinous cost to the state.

sentences.zh: 其暉映千祀，聲芳不絕，夫何為哉？

translations.literal: Their radiance shines across a thousand generations; their repute and fragrance never cease—what is the reason for this?
translations.idiomatic: Their light still shines across a thousand years, and their good name has never faded—how was this achieved?

sentences.zh: 用此道也。

translations.literal: It was by employing this method.
translations.idiomatic: They achieved it by following this way of governance.

sentences.zh: 然則五帝、三王不易人而化，皆在所由化之而已。

translations.literal: Thus the Five Emperors and Three Kings transformed the people without changing the people themselves—all depended solely on those through whom they were transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Even the Five Emperors and Three Kings transformed the people without replacing the people themselves: everything depended on the character of those who did the transforming.

sentences.zh: 故有無能之吏，無不可化之人。

translations.literal: Therefore there may be incapable officials, but there are no people who cannot be transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Hence there can be incompetent magistrates, but there is no populace that cannot be transformed.

sentences.zh: 高祖膺運撫圖，除凶靜亂，日旰忘食，思邁前王。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu received the mandate, took hold of the realm, eliminated the vicious and quelled disorder, forgot to eat until the sun set, and sought to surpass the former kings.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu received Heaven's mandate and seized the throne, he rooted out the wicked and pacified chaos, working until sunset without pausing to eat, determined to outdo the rulers who came before him.

sentences.zh: 然不敦詩書，不尚道德，專任法令，嚴察臨下。

translations.literal: Yet he did not promote the Odes and Documents, did not esteem morality, relied exclusively on laws and ordinances, and governed subordinates with harsh scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he did not cultivate the classics or elevate moral teaching; he relied solely on statute law and watched his subordinates with relentless severity.

sentences.zh: 吏存苟免，罕聞寬惠，乘時射利者，多以一切求名。

translations.literal: Officials merely sought to avoid blame; little was heard of lenience and kindness; those who seized the moment to pursue profit mostly sought renown through rigid expedients.
translations.idiomatic: Officials sought only to escape blame; acts of genuine leniency were rare; and those who exploited the times for gain usually pursued reputation through harsh, ad hoc measures.

sentences.zh: 既煬帝嗣興，志存遠略，車轍馬跡，將遍天下，綱紀馳紊，四維不張。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, his mind was set on far-reaching schemes; chariot tracks and horse prints were about to cover the entire realm; regulations ran wild and were out of order, and the four cardinal bonds were not upheld.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yang came to the throne, bent on vast ambitions, his armies' tracks and horses' hoofprints seemed set to cover the entire world; discipline fell apart, and the fundamental bonds of society collapsed.

sentences.zh: 其或善於侵漁，強於剝割，絕億兆之命，遂一人之求者，謂之奉公，即時升擢。

translations.literal: Those skilled at encroaching and squeezing, strong in stripping and cutting, cutting off the lives of hundreds of millions to satisfy one man's desires—were called dutiful to the public and were promptly promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Officials skilled at squeezing the populace and ruthless in extracting levies—who sacrificed multitudes to satisfy a single man's wishes—were praised as serving the public interest and promoted at once.

sentences.zh: 其或顧名節，存綱紀，抑奪攘之心，以從百姓之欲者，則謂之附下，旋及誅夷。

translations.literal: Those who cared for reputation and integrity, preserved regulations and discipline, checked covetous and rapacious hearts to follow the people's desires—were called partisans of subordinates and soon met with execution and extermination.
translations.idiomatic: Those who guarded their integrity, upheld proper governance, restrained greedy impulses, and yielded to the people's needs were denounced as pandering to the masses and swiftly punished with death.

sentences.zh: 夫吏之侵漁，得其所欲，雖重其禁，猶或為之。

translations.literal: When officials encroach and squeeze, gaining what they desire—even if prohibitions are severe—they may still do it.
translations.idiomatic: When corruption rewards an official with what he wants, he will commit it even under the heaviest penalties.

sentences.zh: 吏之清平，失其所欲，雖崇其賞，猶或不為。

translations.literal: When officials are pure and equitable but lose what they desire—even if rewards are lofty—they may still refuse to act.
translations.idiomatic: When integrity costs an official what he wants, he may refuse to act even when rewards are generous.

sentences.zh: 況於上賞其奸，下得其欲，求得廉潔，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: How much more when above rewards their wickedness and below they obtain their desires—is it not difficult to seek integrity and purity!
translations.idiomatic: When the throne rewarded ruthlessness and subordinates got what they coveted, how difficult could it have been to obtain honest officials!

sentences.zh: 彥光等立嚴察之朝，屬昏狂之主，執心平允，終行仁恕，餘風遺愛，沒而不忘，寬惠之音，足以傳于來葉。

translations.literal: Yanguang and others stood in an age of harsh scrutiny, served a benighted and frantic sovereign, held fast to fair-minded balance, ultimately practiced benevolence and forbearance; their residual influence and enduring kindness, not forgotten after death—their reputation for lenience and kindness can suffice to be transmitted to future generations.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Yanguang served under a regime of harsh scrutiny and a reckless emperor, yet they remained fair-minded and ultimately practiced humane governance. Their lingering goodwill was remembered after death, and their reputation for mercy was enough to echo through generations yet to come.

sentences.zh: 故列其行事，以系《循吏》之篇爾。

translations.literal: Therefore their deeds are listed to attach to the "Biographies of Upright Officials."
translations.idiomatic: I therefore record their deeds in this chapter on upright officials.

sentences.zh: 梁彥光，字修芝，安定烏氏人也。

translations.literal: Liang Yanguang, styled Xiuzhi, was a native of Wushi in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yanguang, whose courtesy name was Xiuzhi, came from Wushi in Anding commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖茂，魏秦、華二州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mao was regional inspector of Qin and Hua in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mao had served as regional inspector of Qin and Hua under the Wei.

sentences.zh: 父顯，周邢州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Xian was inspector of Xingzhou in Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xian had been inspector of Xingzhou under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 彥光少岐嶷，有至性，其父每謂所親曰：「此兒有風骨，當興吾宗。」

translations.literal: Yanguang in youth was precocious and possessed utmost sincerity; his father often said to those close to him: "This boy has spirit and backbone; he will revive our clan."
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Yanguang was unusually sharp and deeply dutiful; his father often told those close to him, "This child has real mettle and will restore our house."

sentences.zh: 七歲時，父遇篤疾，醫云餌五石可愈。

translations.literal: When he was seven, his father fell gravely ill; the physician said that taking the Five Minerals would cure him.
translations.idiomatic: When he was seven, his father fell gravely ill, and the physician said the Five Minerals prescription could save him.

sentences.zh: 時求紫石英不得。

translations.literal: At the time amethyst could not be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: At the time no amethyst could be found.

sentences.zh: 彥光憂瘁不知所為，忽於園中見一物，彥光所不識，怪而持歸，即紫石英也。

translations.literal: Yanguang, anxious and distressed, did not know what to do; suddenly in the garden he saw an object he did not recognize, wondered at it and brought it back—it was amethyst.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang was frantic with worry and at a loss; then in the garden he noticed something unfamiliar, picked it up in wonder, and found it was amethyst.

sentences.zh: 親屬咸異之，以為至孝所感。

translations.literal: Relatives were all astonished and took it as moved by utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His kin were all astonished and took it as a response to his extraordinary filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 魏大統末，入太學，略涉經史，有規檢，造次必以禮。

translations.literal: At the end of Western Wei's Datong era he entered the Imperial Academy, briefly studied the classics and histories, had self-discipline, and in every action invariably observed ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Western Wei's Datong era he entered the Imperial Academy, gained a modest grounding in the classics and histories, conducted himself with discipline, and never departed from propriety even in haste.

sentences.zh: 解褐秘書郎，時年十七。

translations.literal: He doffed commoner's dress as Secretariat Gentleman at age seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: He received his first appointment as Secretariat Gentleman at the age of seventeen.

sentences.zh: 周受禪，遷舍人上士。

translations.literal: When Zhou received the abdication, he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman, Senior Rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou dynasty was founded he was promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the senior rank.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，累遷小馭下大夫。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wu he was repeatedly promoted to Junior Master of Transport, Lower Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu he rose through several posts to Junior Master of Transport, Lower Grandee.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職，毀瘁過禮。

translations.literal: On his mother's death he left office; his grief and emaciation exceeded the rites.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he left office and mourned with a grief that exceeded ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 未幾，起令視事，帝見其毀甚，嗟歎久之，頻蒙慰諭。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled to resume duties; the emperor saw how greatly he was wasted, sighed long, and repeatedly bestowed consolation and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled to duty; the emperor saw how wasted he had become, sighed at length, and repeatedly offered him consolation.

sentences.zh: 後轉小內史下大夫。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Junior Palace Scribe, Lower Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Junior Palace Scribe, Lower Grandee.

sentences.zh: 建德中，為御正下大夫。

translations.literal: During Jiande he served as Junior Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Lower Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiande era he served as Junior Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Lower Grandee.

sentences.zh: 從帝平齊，以功授開府、陽城縣公，邑千戶。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor in pacifying Qi and for merit was granted Opening of a Government Office and made Duke of Yangcheng county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor in the conquest of Qi and, for his merit, was granted the privilege of an independent office and enfeoffed as Duke of Yangcheng with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，拜華州刺史，進封華陽郡公，增邑五百戶，以陽城公轉封一子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, he was appointed inspector of Huazhou, advanced to Duke of Huayang commandery, fief increased by five hundred households, and one son was transferred the enfeoffment of Duke of Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan came to the throne, Yanguang was appointed inspector of Huazhou, advanced to Duke of Huayang commandery with an additional five hundred households in his fief, and one son received the transferred title of Duke of Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 尋進位上大將軍，遷御正上大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Grand General of the Upper Rank and transferred to Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Upper Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to Grand General of the Upper Rank and transferred to Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Upper Grandee.

sentences.zh: 俄拜柱國、青州刺史，屬帝崩，不之官。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Pillar of the State and inspector of Qingzhou; as the emperor died, he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Pillar of the State and inspector of Qingzhou, but the emperor died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 及高祖受禪，以為岐州刺史，兼領岐州宮監，增邑五百戶，通前二千戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, he was made inspector of Qizhou and concurrently overseer of the Qizhou palace establishment, fief increased by five hundred households, totaling two thousand households with the previous.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu founded the Sui dynasty, Yanguang was appointed inspector of Qizhou and concurrently overseer of the Qizhou palace establishment, with his fief increased by five hundred households to two thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 甚有惠政，嘉禾連理，出於州境，

translations.literal: He had very benevolent administration; auspicious grain with conjoined stalks appeared within the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His benevolent rule was remarkable; within the prefecture appeared auspicious grain with conjoined stalks.

sentences.zh: 開皇二年，上幸岐州，悅其能，乃下詔曰：「賞以勸善，義兼訓物。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaihuang, the emperor visited Qizhou, delighted with his ability, and issued an edict saying: "Rewards are to encourage goodness; the principle also instructs the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaihuang, when the emperor visited Qizhou and was pleased with his performance, he issued an edict: "Rewards encourage virtue and also teach the people by example.

sentences.zh: 彥光操履平直，識用凝遠，布政岐下，威惠在人，廉慎之譽，聞於天下。

translations.literal: Yanguang's conduct and bearing are upright and level, his insight and employment profound and far-reaching; he deployed administration below Qi, authority and kindness among the people; his reputation for integrity and caution is heard throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang's conduct is upright, his judgment far-sighted; in governing Qi he has won both respect and affection, and his reputation for integrity is known throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 三載之後，自當遷陟，恐其匱乏，且宜旌善。

translations.literal: After three years he will naturally be promoted and transferred; fearing he may be in want, it is fitting for now to commend his goodness.
translations.idiomatic: In three years he will naturally be promoted; lest he be in want before then, it is fitting now to reward his excellence.

sentences.zh: 可賜粟五百斛，物三百段，御傘一枚，庶使有感朕心，日增其美。

translations.literal: He may be granted five hundred hu of grain, three hundred bolts of goods, and one imperial parasol, so that he may be moved by Our heart and daily increase his excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Let him receive five hundred hu of grain, three hundred bolts of goods, and one imperial parasol, so that he may feel Our regard and strive ever harder to excel.

sentences.zh: 四海之內，凡曰官人，慕高山而仰止，聞清風而自勵。」

translations.literal: Within the four seas, all who are called officials should admire the high mountain and gaze upward, hear the clear wind and encourage themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the realm, every official should take him as a lofty peak to admire and a fresh breeze to stir his own resolve."

sentences.zh: 未幾，又賜錢五萬。

translations.literal: Before long he was again granted fifty thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was granted fifty thousand cash as well.

sentences.zh: 後數歲，轉相州刺史。

translations.literal: Several years later he was transferred to inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was transferred to inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 彥光前在岐州，其俗頗質，以靜鎮之，合境大化，奏課連最，為天下第一。

translations.literal: When Yanguang had previously been in Qizhou, its customs were rather plain; he governed them with tranquility, the whole territory was greatly transformed, his memorial assessments were repeatedly top, and he was first under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: At Qizhou, where the people were comparatively straightforward, he governed with quiet steadiness, transformed the entire prefecture, and ranked first in the realm in successive performance reports.

sentences.zh: 及居相部，如岐州法。

translations.literal: When he resided in the Xiang region, he applied the Qizhou method.
translations.idiomatic: When he took up office in the Xiang region, he governed by the same methods he had used at Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 鄴都雜俗，人多變詐，為之作歌，稱其不能理化。

translations.literal: The mixed customs of the Ye capital—many people were changeable and deceitful—made songs about him, saying he could not transform and educate.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was a place of mixed and shifting customs, and many of its people were cunning; they composed songs mocking him as unable to transform society.

sentences.zh: 上聞而譴之，竟坐免。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and reprimanded him; in the end he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this, he rebuked Yanguang and ultimately dismissed him from office.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，拜趙州刺史，彥光言於上曰：「臣前待罪相州，百姓呼為戴帽餳。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed inspector of Zhaozhou; Yanguang said to the emperor: "Your servant previously awaited punishment at Xiangzhou; the people called me Hat-wearing Cake.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he was appointed inspector of Zhaozhou and said to the emperor, "When I was disgraced at Xiangzhou, the people nicknamed me 'the Hat-wearing Cake'.

sentences.zh: 臣自分廢黜，無復衣冠之望，不謂天恩復垂收采。

translations.literal: Your servant considered himself dismissed and ruined, with no further hope of official rank; he did not expect Heaven's grace again to extend acceptance and employment.
translations.idiomatic: I had resigned myself to permanent disgrace and never expected Your Majesty to employ me again.

sentences.zh: 請復為相州，改弦易調，庶有以變其風俗，上答隆恩。」

translations.literal: I beg to return to Xiangzhou, change the strings and alter the tuning, so that I may thereby transform its customs and repay from above the profound grace."
translations.idiomatic: I beg to be sent back to Xiangzhou so that I may change my methods, transform its customs, and repay Your Majesty's great kindness."

sentences.zh: 上從之，復為相州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor consented and again made him inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and reappointed him inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 豪猾者聞彥光自請而來，莫不嗤笑。

translations.literal: The powerful and cunning, hearing that Yanguang had asked to come of himself, all sneered and laughed.
translations.idiomatic: When the local bullies heard that Yanguang had asked to return, they all laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 彥光下車，發摘奸隱，有若神明，於是狡猾之徒，莫不潛竄，合境大駭。

translations.literal: When Yanguang dismounted from his carriage, he exposed and seized hidden wrongdoing like a spirit; thus the crafty sort all secretly fled, and the whole territory was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Yanguang took office he uncovered hidden crimes with uncanny precision; the crafty fled in secret, and the whole prefecture was stunned.

sentences.zh: 初，齊亡後，衣冠士人多遷關內，唯技巧、商販及樂戶之家移實州郭。

translations.literal: At first, after Qi's fall, gentry and scholar-officials mostly moved within the passes; only families of artisans, merchants, and musician households were relocated to fill the prefectural cities.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Qi, most gentry and scholar-officials had moved west of the passes; only artisans, merchants, and households of registered performers had been settled in the prefectural towns.

sentences.zh: 由是人情險詖，妄起風謠，訴訟官人，萬端千變。

translations.literal: Hence human sentiments were treacherous and perverse; groundless rumors arose; lawsuits against officials multiplied in countless shifting forms.
translations.idiomatic: As a result the populace had grown treacherous, rumors spread without cause, and lawsuits against officials multiplied in endless variation.

sentences.zh: 彥光欲革其弊，乃用秩俸之物，招致山東大儒，每鄉立學，非聖哲之書不得教授。

translations.literal: Yanguang wished to reform these abuses; he therefore used items from his salary and stipend to summon great Confucians from east of the mountains, established schools in every district, and no books except those of sages and worthies might be taught.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to reform these abuses, Yanguang spent his official salary to invite eminent Confucian scholars from the east, founded a school in every district, and permitted instruction only in the classics of the sages.

sentences.zh: 常以季月召集之，親臨策試。

translations.literal: He regularly in the seasonal months summoned them and personally came to conduct written examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Each season he gathered the students and personally presided over their examinations.

sentences.zh: 有勤學異等、聰令有聞者，升堂設饌，其餘並坐廊下。

translations.literal: Those diligent in study of outstanding grade and known for clever talent were raised to the hall and given a feast; the rest all sat in the corridor below.
translations.idiomatic: Students who studied diligently and showed exceptional promise were invited into the hall and served a proper meal; the rest sat in the corridor.

sentences.zh: 有好諍訟、惰業無成者，坐之庭中，設以草具。

translations.literal: Those fond of quarreling in lawsuits, idle in studies and achieving nothing, were seated in the courtyard and given coarse fare.
translations.idiomatic: Those who quarreled habitually or idled without progress were seated in the courtyard and given only coarse food.

sentences.zh: 及大成，當舉行賓貢之禮，又于郊外祖道，並以財物資之。

translations.literal: When they had completed their studies and were to undergo the guest-tribute rites, he also at the outskirts performed the farewell ceremony and supplied them all with goods and wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When students completed their studies and were ready for the tribute examinations, he held a farewell ceremony outside the city and provided them with travel funds.

sentences.zh: 於是人皆克勵，風俗大改。

translations.literal: Thereupon everyone restrained and encouraged themselves; customs were greatly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter everyone applied himself, and local customs were thoroughly transformed.

sentences.zh: 有滏陽人焦通，性酗酒，事親禮闕，為從弟所訟。

translations.literal: There was a man of Fuyang named Jiao Tong, by nature addicted to wine, deficient in ritual toward his parents, sued by his younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Fuyang named Jiao Tong was a heavy drinker who neglected his duties toward his parents and was sued by a younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 彥光弗之罪，將至州學，令觀於孔子廟。

translations.literal: Yanguang did not punish him; he was brought to the prefectural school and ordered to observe in the Confucius temple.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang did not punish him but had him brought to the prefectural school and shown the Confucius temple.

sentences.zh: 于時廟中有韓伯瑜，母杖不痛，哀母力弱，對母悲泣之像，通遂感悟，既悲且愧，若無自容。

translations.literal: At the time in the temple was an image of Han Boyu—when his mother beat him he did not feel pain, grieving that his mother's strength was weak, facing his mother weeping in sorrow; Tong thereupon was awakened, both grieved and ashamed, as if he had no place for himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the temple stood an image of Han Boyu, who did not flinch when his mother beat him because he grieved that she had grown weak, and wept before her; Tong was deeply moved, filled with sorrow and shame, and could hardly bear to look at himself.

sentences.zh: 彥光訓諭而遣之。

translations.literal: Yanguang instructed and admonished him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang admonished him and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 後改過勵行，卒為善士。

translations.literal: Later he reformed his faults and encouraged his conduct, and ultimately became a good man.
translations.idiomatic: He later reformed his ways and in the end became a respectable man.

sentences.zh: 以德化人，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Transforming people through virtue—all were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His transformation of the people through moral example was always of this kind.

sentences.zh: 吏人感悅，略無諍訟。

translations.literal: Officials and people were moved and pleased; scarcely any contentious lawsuits remained.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners alike were moved with gratitude, and lawsuits all but disappeared.

sentences.zh: 後數歲，卒官，時年六十。

translations.literal: Several years later he died in office at age sixty.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he died in office at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 贈冀、定、青、瀛四州刺史，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the four prefectures of Ji, Ding, Qing, and Ying as inspector titles; his posthumous name was Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored with the titles of inspector of Ji, Ding, Qing, and Ying, and given the posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 子文謙嗣。

translations.literal: His son Wenqian succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wenqian succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 文謙弘雅有父風，以上柱國嫡子，例授儀同，

translations.literal: Wenqian was magnanimous and refined, with his father's manner; as legitimate son of an Upper Pillar of the State, by precedent he was granted Commissioner with Equal Status.
translations.idiomatic: Wenqian was cultivated and gracious and bore his father's manner; as the legitimate son of an Upper Pillar of the State, he was granted the rank of Commissioner with Equal Status by precedent.

sentences.zh: 開皇十五年，拜上州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kaihuang, he was appointed inspector of Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Kaihuang, he was appointed inspector of Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，轉饒州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he was transferred to inspector of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, he was transferred to inspector of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，為鄱陽太守，稱為天下之最。

translations.literal: After more than a year he became governor of Poyang and was acclaimed as foremost under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a year he became governor of Poyang and was acclaimed the finest administrator in the realm.

sentences.zh: 征拜戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court and appointed Vice Minister of the Household.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，領武賁郎將，尋以本官兼檢校太府、衛尉二少卿。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he led as Brave Attendant General; soon with his original office he concurrently inspected the Grand Treasury and Palace Guard, both as Junior Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign he served as Brave Attendant General and soon afterward concurrently supervised the Grand Treasury and the Palace Guard as their junior minister.

sentences.zh: 明年，又領武賁郎將，為盧龍道軍副。

translations.literal: The next year he again led as Brave Attendant General and served as deputy commander of the Lulong Route army.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he again served as Brave Attendant General and as deputy commander of the Lulong Route army.

sentences.zh: 會楊玄感作亂，其弟武賁郎將玄縱先隸文謙，玄感反問未至而玄縱逃走，文謙不之覺，坐是配防桂林而卒，時年五十六。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, his younger brother Brave Attendant General Xuanzong had previously been under Wenqian's command; Xuangan's inquiry of rebellion had not yet arrived when Xuanzong fled; Wenqian did not detect it; for this he was sentenced to garrison duty at Guilin and died there at age fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, his younger brother Xuanzong, a Brave Attendant General who had served under Wenqian, fled before word of the revolt arrived; Wenqian failed to notice, was sentenced to garrison duty at Guilin, and died there at the age of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 少子文讓，初封陽城縣公，後為鷹揚郎將。

translations.literal: The younger son Wenrang was first enfeoffed as Duke of Yangcheng county and later served as Soaring Hawk General.
translations.idiomatic: The younger son Wenrang was first enfeoffed as Duke of Yangcheng and later served as Soaring Hawk General.

sentences.zh: 從衛玄擊楊玄感於東都，力戰而死，贈通議大夫。

translations.literal: He followed Wei Xuan in attacking Yang Xuangan at the Eastern Capital, fought fiercely and died, and was posthumously granted Grand Master for Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Wei Xuan in the attack on Yang Xuangan at the Eastern Capital, fought fiercely until he was killed, and was posthumously granted the title Grand Master for Discussion.

sentences.zh: 樊叔略，陳留人也。

translations.literal: Fan Shulue, a man of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shulue was a native of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 父歡，仕魏為南兗州刺史、阿陽侯。

translations.literal: His father Huan served Wei as regional inspector of Southern Yanzhou and Marquis of Ayang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huan had served the Wei as regional inspector of Southern Yanzhou and Marquis of Ayang.

sentences.zh: 屬高氏專權，將謀興復之計，為高氏所誅。

translations.literal: When the Gao clan monopolized power, he was about to plot a plan to restore the dynasty and was executed by the Gao clan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gao clan seized power, he plotted to restore the dynasty and was executed by them.

sentences.zh: 叔略時在髫齔，遂被腐刑，給使殿省。

translations.literal: Shulue was then in infancy and was subjected to castration, assigned to serve in the palace directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Shulue was still a child and was castrated, then assigned to serve in the palace directorate.

sentences.zh: 身長九尺，志氣不凡，頗為高氏所忌。

translations.literal: His body was nine chi in height, his spirit and ambition extraordinary; he was rather feared by the Gao clan.
translations.idiomatic: He stood nine chi tall, possessed an uncommon spirit, and was regarded with suspicion by the Gao clan.

sentences.zh: 內不自安，遂奔關西。

translations.literal: Inwardly ill at ease, he fled to west of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling unsafe, he fled west of the passes.

sentences.zh: 周太祖見而器之，引置左右。

translations.literal: Zhou's founding emperor saw him and valued him, drawing him to his side.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou founding emperor took notice of him, valued his ability, and kept him at his side.

sentences.zh: 尋授都督，襲爵為侯。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Area Commander and inherited the title as Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Area Commander and inherited his father's marquisate.

sentences.zh: 大塚宰宇文護執政，引為中尉。

translations.literal: When Grand Minister Yuwen Hu held power, he was brought in as Central Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Minister Yuwen Hu held power, Shulue was appointed Central Commandant.

sentences.zh: 叔略多計數，曉習時事，護漸委信之，兼督內外。

translations.literal: Shulue had many stratagems and understood current affairs; Hu gradually entrusted him and had him oversee both inner and outer affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shulue was resourceful and well versed in current affairs; Hu gradually entrusted him with authority over both palace and government affairs.

sentences.zh: 累遷驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and Opening of a Government Office with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to General of Agile Cavalry and Opening of a Government Office with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 護誅後，齊王憲引為園苑監。

translations.literal: After Hu was executed, Prince of Qi Xian brought him in as Director of Parks and Gardens.
translations.idiomatic: After Hu was executed, Prince Xian of Qi appointed him Director of Parks and Gardens.

sentences.zh: 時憲素有吞關東之志，叔略因事數進兵謀，憲甚奇之，

translations.literal: At the time Xian had long harbored the ambition to swallow the east of the mountains; Shulue on occasion repeatedly advanced military plans, and Xian greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian had long wished to conquer the east of the mountains; Shulue repeatedly offered him military counsel, and the prince came to admire him greatly.

sentences.zh: 建德五年，從武帝伐齊，叔略部率精銳，每戰身先士卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiande, he followed Emperor Wu in attacking Qi; Shulue's division led elite troops, and in every battle he took the lead before the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jiande, when he followed Emperor Wu in the campaign against Qi, Shulue led elite troops and in every battle placed himself at the front of his men.

sentences.zh: 以功加上開府，進封清鄉縣公，邑千四百戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced to Upper Opening of a Government Office, promoted to Duke of Qingxiang county with a fief of fourteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to Upper Opening of a Government Office and enfeoffed as Duke of Qingxiang with a fief of fourteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 拜汴州刺史，號為明決。

translations.literal: He was appointed inspector of Bianzhou and was known as clear and decisive.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed inspector of Bianzhou and gained a reputation for clarity and decisiveness.

sentences.zh: 宣帝時，于洛陽營建東京，以叔略有巧思，拜營構監，宮室制度，皆叔略所定。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xuan, when the Eastern Capital was built at Luoyang, because Shulue had ingenious ideas he was appointed Director of Construction; the palace regulations were all set by Shulue.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan, when the Eastern Capital was built at Luoyang, Shulue's ingenuity won him appointment as Director of Construction, and the palace layout was entirely his design.

sentences.zh: 功未就而帝崩。

translations.literal: The work was not completed when the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: The project was still unfinished when the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 尉迥之亂，高祖令叔略鎮大樑。

translations.literal: In the rebellion of Yu Chi, Emperor Gaozu ordered Shulue to garrison Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: During Yu Chi's rebellion, Emperor Gaozu ordered Shulue to hold Daliang.

sentences.zh: 迥將宇文威來寇，叔略擊走之。

translations.literal: Jiong's general Yuwen Wei came to attack; Shulue struck and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiong's general Yuwen Wei attacked, Shulue defeated and drove him away.

sentences.zh: 以功拜大將軍，復為汴州刺史。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed Grand General and again made inspector of Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was appointed Grand General and again made inspector of Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，加位上大將軍，進爵安定郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, he was advanced to Grand General of the Upper Rank and promoted to Duke of Anding commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu founded the Sui dynasty, Shulue was promoted to Grand General of the Upper Rank and enfeoffed as Duke of Anding commandery.

sentences.zh: 在州數年，甚有聲譽。

translations.literal: In the prefecture for several years he had a very fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He served several years in the prefecture and earned an outstanding reputation.

sentences.zh: 鄴都俗薄，號曰難化，朝廷以叔略所在著稱，遷相州刺史，政為當時第一。

translations.literal: The customs of the Ye capital were shallow and called hard to transform; the court, because Shulue's whereabouts were renowned, transferred him to inspector of Xiangzhou, and his administration was first of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was known for shallow customs and was considered hard to govern; because Shulue's reputation preceded him, the court transferred him to Xiangzhou, where his administration ranked first in the realm.

sentences.zh: 上降璽書褒美之，賜物三百段，粟五百石，班示天下。

translations.literal: The emperor sent down an imperial letter praising him, granted three hundred bolts of goods and five hundred shi of grain, and circulated the announcement throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an imperial letter praising him, granted three hundred bolts of goods and five hundred shi of grain, and proclaimed the reward throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 百姓為之語曰：「智無窮，清鄉公。

translations.literal: The people made a saying about him: "Wisdom without end—the Duke of Qingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: The people composed a saying: "Wisdom without end—the Duke of Qingxiang.

sentences.zh: 上下正，樊安定。」

translations.literal: Above and below upright—Fan of Anding."
translations.idiomatic: Above and below made upright—Fan of Anding."

sentences.zh: 征拜司農卿，吏人莫不流涕，相與立碑頌其德政。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of the Grand Granary; officials and people all wept, and together they erected a stele praising his virtuous administration.
translations.idiomatic: When he was summoned to serve as Minister of the Grand Granary, officials and commoners wept; together they erected a stele praising his benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 自為司農，凡種植，叔略別為條制，皆出人意表。

translations.literal: From the time he became Minister of the Grand Granary, for all planting Shulue separately made regulations, all beyond people's expectations.
translations.idiomatic: As Minister of the Grand Granary, he devised planting regulations that surprised everyone with their ingenuity.

sentences.zh: 朝廷有疑滯，公卿所未能決者，叔略輒為評理。

translations.literal: When the court had doubts and delays that the excellencies could not resolve, Shulue would assess and settle them.
translations.idiomatic: When the court faced unresolved questions that even the highest ministers could not settle, Shulue would adjudicate them.

sentences.zh: 雖無學術，有所依據，然師心獨見，暗與理合。

translations.literal: Although without scholarly learning he had something to rely on, yet following his own mind with unique insight, he tacitly accorded with principle.
translations.idiomatic: Though he lacked formal scholarly training, his judgments rested on sound instinct and quietly accorded with reason.

sentences.zh: 甚為上所親委，高熲、楊素亦禮遇之。

translations.literal: He was greatly trusted and entrusted by the emperor; Gao Jiong and Yang Su also treated him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relied on him heavily; Gao Jiong and Yang Su also treated him with respect.

sentences.zh: 叔略雖為司農，往往參督九卿事。

translations.literal: Although Shulue was Minister of the Grand Granary, he often participated in and oversaw the affairs of the Nine Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Although his title was Minister of the Grand Granary, he often supervised the affairs of the other chief ministers as well.

sentences.zh: 性頗豪侈，每食必方丈，備水陸。

translations.literal: His nature was rather extravagant; every meal had to fill a square zhang, with delicacies from land and water prepared.
translations.idiomatic: He was rather extravagant by nature; every meal had to be lavish, with delicacies from land and sea.

sentences.zh: 十四年，從祠太山，行至洛陽，上令錄囚徒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he followed in sacrificing at Mount Tai; when he reached Luoyang the emperor ordered him to record the prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he accompanied the emperor to sacrifice at Mount Tai; when they reached Luoyang, the emperor ordered him to review the prisoners.

sentences.zh: 具狀將奏，晨起，至獄門，於馬上暴卒，時年五十九。

translations.literal: Having prepared the report and about to memorialize, he rose in the morning, reached the prison gate, and suddenly died on his horse at age fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He had prepared his report and was about to present it; early in the morning, as he reached the prison gate, he suddenly died in the saddle at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 上悼惜久之，贈亳州刺史，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned and regretted him for a long time, posthumously granted him inspector of Bozhou, and gave the posthumous name Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him at length, posthumously honored him as inspector of Bozhou, and gave him the posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 趙軌，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Gui, a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gui was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 父肅，魏廷尉卿。

translations.literal: His father Su was Commandant of Justice in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Su had served the Wei as Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 軌少好學，有行檢。

translations.literal: Gui in youth loved learning and had self-discipline.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Gui loved learning and conducted himself with discipline.

sentences.zh: 周蔡王引為記室，以清苦聞。

translations.literal: The Zhou Prince of Cai brought him in as Recorder and he became known for purity and hardship.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou Prince of Cai appointed him Recorder, and he became known for his austere integrity.

sentences.zh: 遷衛州治中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Assistant Administrator of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Assistant Administrator of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，轉齊州別駕，有能名。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, he was transferred to Vice Governor of Qizhou and had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu founded the dynasty, Gui was transferred to Vice Governor of Qizhou and earned a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 其東鄰有桑，葚落其家，軌遣人悉拾還其主，誡其諸子曰：「吾非以此求名，意者非機杼之物，不願侵人。

translations.literal: His eastern neighbor had mulberry trees; mulberries fell into his house; Gui sent people to gather them all and return them to the owner, admonishing his sons: "I do not seek reputation by this; in my view, things not from the loom—I am unwilling to encroach on others.
translations.idiomatic: Mulberries from his eastern neighbor's trees fell into his yard; Gui had them all gathered and returned, then told his sons, "I am not doing this for reputation. Things that do not come from one's own labor should never be taken from another.

sentences.zh: 汝等宜以為誡。」

translations.literal: You should take this as a warning."
translations.idiomatic: You should take this as your lesson."

sentences.zh: 在州四年，考績連最。

translations.literal: In the prefecture for four years his performance assessments were repeatedly top.
translations.idiomatic: During four years in office his performance assessments ranked first every year.

sentences.zh: 持節使者郃陽公梁子恭狀上，高祖嘉之，賜物三百段，米三百石，征軌入朝。

translations.literal: The commissioner with credentials, Duke of Heyang Liang Zigong, memorialized upward; Emperor Gaozu commended him, granted three hundred bolts of goods and three hundred shi of rice, and summoned Gui to court.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Liang Zigong, Duke of Heyang, reported his excellence to the throne; Emperor Gaozu commended him, granted three hundred bolts of goods and three hundred shi of rice, and summoned him to court.

sentences.zh: 父老相送者各揮涕曰：「別駕在官，水火不與百姓交，是以不敢以壺酒相送。

translations.literal: The elders who saw him off each wiped away tears and said: "While Vice Governor was in office, he would not accept even fire or water from the people; therefore we dare not send him off with a pot of wine.
translations.idiomatic: The elders who came to see him off wept and said, "While you served as vice governor you would not accept even fire or water from the people, so we dare not send you off with wine.

sentences.zh: 公清若水，請酌一杯水奉餞。」

translations.literal: Your lordship is pure as water; we beg to offer a cup of water as a farewell gift."
translations.idiomatic: You are pure as water; please accept a cup of water as our farewell gift."

sentences.zh: 軌受而飲之。

translations.literal: Gui accepted it and drank.
translations.idiomatic: Gui accepted it and drank.

sentences.zh: 既至京師，詔與奇章公牛弘撰定律令格式。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital, he was ordered together with Niu Hong of Qizhang to compile laws, ordinances, and formats.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the capital, he was ordered to compile laws and administrative formats together with Niu Hong of Qizhang.

sentences.zh: 時衛王爽為原州總管，上見爽年少，以軌所在有聲，授原州總管司馬。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Wei Shuang was overall commander of Yuanzhou; the emperor saw Shuang was young and, because Gui's whereabouts had a fine reputation, appointed him Chief of Staff to the overall commander of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei Shuang was then overall commander of Yuanzhou; seeing that the prince was young and that Gui's reputation was excellent, the emperor appointed Gui his chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 在道夜行，其左右馬逸入田中，暴人禾。

translations.literal: Traveling on the road at night, the horses of his attendants bolted into the fields and trampled people's grain.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling by night, his attendants' horses bolted into the fields and trampled the crops.

sentences.zh: 軌駐馬待明，訪禾主酬直而去。

translations.literal: Gui halted his horse and waited until dawn, sought out the grain's owner, paid compensation, and then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Gui halted until dawn, found the owner of the damaged grain, paid compensation, and then continued on his way.

sentences.zh: 原州人吏聞之，莫不改操。

translations.literal: When the people and officials of Yuanzhou heard of it, none failed to reform their conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When the officials and people of Yuanzhou heard of this, all reformed their conduct.

sentences.zh: 後數年，遷硤州刺史，撫緝萌夷，甚有恩惠。

translations.literal: Several years later he was transferred to inspector of Xiazhou, pacified and soothed the tribal peoples, and had very great kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was transferred to inspector of Xiazhou, where he pacified the tribal peoples with notable kindness.

sentences.zh: 尋轉壽州總管長史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Chief Clerk of the overall command of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to chief clerk under the overall command of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 芍陂舊有五門堰，蕪穢不修。

translations.literal: At Quepi there was formerly the Five-Gate Weir, overgrown and dilapidated and not repaired.
translations.idiomatic: The old Five-Gate Weir at Quepi had fallen into neglect and disrepair.

sentences.zh: 軌於是勸課人吏，更開三十六門，灌田五千餘頃，人賴其利。

translations.literal: Gui thereupon urged and assessed officials and clerks, reopened thirty-six gates, irrigated more than five thousand qing of fields, and the people relied on the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Gui urged his officials to reopen thirty-six sluice gates, irrigate more than five thousand qing of farmland, and bring lasting benefit to the people.

sentences.zh: 秩滿歸鄉里，卒于家，時年六十二。

translations.literal: When his term ended he returned to his home district and died at home at age sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he returned home and died there at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 子弘安、弘智，並知名。

translations.literal: His sons Hong'an and Hongzhi were both well known.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Hong'an and Hongzhi both became well known.

sentences.zh: 房恭懿，字慎言，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Fang Gongyi, styled Shenyan, was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Gongyi, whose courtesy name was Shenyan, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 父謨，齊吏部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Mo was Minister of Personnel in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mo had been Minister of Personnel under the Qi.

sentences.zh: 恭懿性沉深，有局量，達于從政。

translations.literal: Gongyi's nature was deep and reserved; he had breadth of capacity and was adept at participating in government.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi was reserved and measured in temperament, possessed breadth of vision, and was skilled in governance.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，釋褐開府參軍事，曆平恩令、濟陰守，並有能名。

translations.literal: He served Qi, doffed commoner's dress as Staff Officer of the Opening Office, and successively held the posts of magistrate of Ping'en and governor of Jiyin—all with a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qi he received his first appointment as staff officer of an opening office and successively served as magistrate of Ping'en and governor of Jiyin, earning a reputation for competence in each post.

sentences.zh: 會齊亡，不得調。

translations.literal: When Qi fell he could not be transferred.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi fell, he was left without appointment.

sentences.zh: 尉迥之亂，恭懿預焉，迥敗，廢於家。

translations.literal: In the rebellion of Yu Chi, Gongyi participated; when Jiong was defeated, he was dismissed and lived at home.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in Yu Chi's rebellion; when Jiong was defeated, Gongyi was dismissed and lived in retirement.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，吏部尚書蘇威薦之，授新豐令，政為三輔之最。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, Minister of Personnel Su Wei recommended him; he was appointed magistrate of Xinfeng, and his administration was foremost among the Three Assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang era, Minister of Personnel Su Wei recommended him; appointed magistrate of Xinfeng, his administration ranked first among the capital districts.

sentences.zh: 上聞而嘉之，賜物四百段，恭懿以所得賜分給窮乏。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and commended him, granted four hundred bolts of goods, and Gongyi distributed what he received among the poor and destitute.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of this and commended him, granting four hundred bolts of goods, which Gongyi distributed among the poor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復賜米三百石，恭懿又以賑貧人。

translations.literal: Before long he was again granted three hundred shi of rice, and Gongyi again used it to relieve the poor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was granted three hundred shi of rice, which he again used to aid the poor.

sentences.zh: 上聞而止之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this, he ordered him to stop.

sentences.zh: 時雍州諸縣令每朔朝謁，上見恭懿，必呼至榻前，訪以理人之術。

translations.literal: At the time the magistrates of Yongzhou each month at the new moon attended court; when the emperor saw Gongyi he invariably summoned him before the couch and inquired about the methods of governing people.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the magistrates of Yongzhou attended the monthly court audience, the emperor would call Gongyi forward and ask his counsel on governing the people.

sentences.zh: 蘇威重薦之，超授澤州司馬，有異績，賜物百段，良馬一匹。

translations.literal: Su Wei again strongly recommended him; he was exceptionally appointed Chief of Staff of Zezhou, had outstanding achievements, and was granted one hundred bolts of goods and one fine horse.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei recommended him again; he was promoted out of turn to chief of staff of Zezhou, achieved outstanding results, and was granted one hundred bolts of goods and a fine horse.

sentences.zh: 遷德州司馬，在職歲餘，盧愷復奏恭懿政為天下之最。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief of Staff of Dezhou; after more than a year in office, Lu Kai again memorialized that Gongyi's administration was foremost under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to chief of staff of Dezhou, he served a little over a year before Lu Kai again reported that his administration was the finest in the realm.

sentences.zh: 上甚異之，復賜百段，因謂諸州朝集使曰：「如房恭懿志存體國，愛養我百姓，此乃上天宗廟之所佑助，豈朕寡薄能致之乎！

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly struck by this and again granted one hundred bolts, and thereby said to the envoys of the various prefectures attending court: "Such as Fang Gongyi, whose will is set on cherishing the state and who loves and nurtures Our common people—this is what Heaven above and the ancestral temples aid and support; how could Our meager virtue bring it about!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply impressed and granted another hundred bolts, then told the envoys from the prefectures, "Men like Fang Gongyi, who devote themselves to the state's welfare and cherish my people—this is Heaven's blessing, not something my meager virtue alone could produce!

sentences.zh: 朕即拜為刺史。

translations.literal: We shall at once appoint him regional inspector.
translations.idiomatic: I shall appoint him regional inspector at once.

sentences.zh: 豈止為一州而已，當今天下模範之，卿等宜師學也。」

translations.literal: It is not only for one prefecture; he should be the model for all under Heaven today—you should take him as teacher and learn."
translations.idiomatic: This is not for one prefecture alone—he should be the model for the entire realm, and all of you should learn from him."

sentences.zh: 上又曰：「房恭懿所在之處，百姓視之如父母。

translations.literal: The emperor also said: "Wherever Fang Gongyi is, the common people regard him as father and mother.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor added, "Wherever Fang Gongyi serves, the people regard him as a parent.

sentences.zh: 朕若置之而不賞，上天宗廟其當責我。

translations.literal: If We place him in office and do not reward him, Heaven above and the ancestral temples will surely hold Us accountable.
translations.idiomatic: If I fail to reward such a man, Heaven and my ancestors will hold me accountable.

sentences.zh: 內外官人宜知我意。」

translations.literal: Officials within and without should know Our intent."
translations.idiomatic: Let all officials within and without the court understand my intent."

sentences.zh: 於是下詔曰：「德州司馬房恭懿出宰百里，毗贊二籓，善政能官，標映倫伍。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued: "Chief of Staff of Dezhou Fang Gongyi went out to govern a hundred li, assisted two principalities, had good administration and ability as an official, and stands out among his peers.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "Fang Gongyi of Dezhou has governed at the local level and assisted two principalities with outstanding ability, distinguishing himself among his peers.

sentences.zh: 班條按部，實允僉屬，委以方嶽，聲實俱美。

translations.literal: In promulgating regulations and inspecting departments, he truly won the assent of subordinates; entrusted with a territorial command, his reputation and substance are both excellent.
translations.idiomatic: In administering regulations and inspecting departments he has won universal approval; entrusted with a territorial command, his reputation and achievement are equally excellent.

sentences.zh: 可使持節海州諸軍事、海州刺史。」

translations.literal: He may be made Commissioner with Credentials for all military affairs of Haizhou and inspector of Haizhou."
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed Commissioner with Credentials for all military affairs of Haizhou and inspector of Haizhou."

sentences.zh: 未幾，會國子博士何妥奏恭懿尉迥之黨，不當仕進，威、愷二人朋黨，曲相薦舉。

translations.literal: Before long, the Erudite of the National University He Tuo memorialized that Gongyi was a partisan of Yu Chi, unfit for advancement in office, and that Wei and Kai were a faction curving to recommend each other.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Erudite He Tuo of the National University accused Gongyi of being a partisan of Yu Chi and unfit for office, and charged Su Wei and Lu Kai with forming a faction to promote him improperly.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，恭懿竟得罪，配防嶺南。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged; Gongyi in the end was found guilty and sentenced to garrison duty in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious; Gongyi was convicted and sentenced to garrison duty in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，征還京師，行至洪州，遇患卒。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned back to the capital; when he reached Hongzhou he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to the capital but fell ill and died at Hongzhou on the way.

sentences.zh: 論者於今冤之。

translations.literal: Commentators to this day regard him as wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators still regard his case as a grave injustice.

sentences.zh: 公孫景茂，字元蔚，河間阜城人也。

translations.literal: Gongsun Jingmao, styled Yuanwei, was a man of Fucheng in Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Jingmao, whose courtesy name was Yuanwei, came from Fucheng in Hejian commandery.

sentences.zh: 容貌魁梧，少好學，博涉經史。

translations.literal: His appearance was tall and imposing; in youth he loved learning and broadly studied the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Tall and imposing in appearance, he loved learning as a youth and gained a broad knowledge of the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 在魏，察孝廉，射策甲科，為襄城王長史，兼行參軍。

translations.literal: In Wei he was examined as Filial and Incorrupt, achieved first rank in the target-shooting examination, and served as Chief Clerk to the Prince of Xiangcheng and concurrently Acting Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Wei he was nominated as Filial and Incorrupt, ranked first in the civil examination, and served as chief clerk to the Prince of Xiangcheng and concurrently acting staff officer.

sentences.zh: 遷太常博士，多所損益，時人稱為書庫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Erudite of the Grand Ceremonial; he made many additions and deletions, and people of the time called him a library of books.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Erudite of the Grand Ceremonial, he revised many ritual texts, and contemporaries called him a walking library.

sentences.zh: 後曆高唐令、大理正，俱有能名。

translations.literal: Later he successively held the posts of magistrate of Gaotang and Rectifier of the Grand Court of Justice, both with a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as magistrate of Gaotang and rectifier of the Grand Court of Justice, earning a reputation for ability in each post.

sentences.zh: 及齊滅，周武帝聞而召見，與語器之，授濟北太守。

translations.literal: When Qi was destroyed, Emperor Wu of Zhou heard of him and summoned him for an audience; in conversation he valued him and appointed him governor of Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Qi, Emperor Wu of Zhou summoned him, was impressed in conversation, and appointed him governor of Jibei.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職。

translations.literal: On his mother's death he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，詔征入朝，訪以政術，拜汝南太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was ordered summoned to court, questioned on methods of government, and appointed governor of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang era he was summoned to court, consulted on methods of governance, and appointed governor of Runan.

sentences.zh: 郡廢，轉曹州司馬。

translations.literal: When the commandery was abolished, he was transferred to Chief of Staff of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the commandery was abolished, he was transferred to chief of staff of Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 在職數年，以老病乞骸骨，優詔不許。

translations.literal: In office for several years, on grounds of age and illness he begged to return his bones; a gracious edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in office he requested retirement on grounds of age and illness, but a gracious edict refused permission.

sentences.zh: 俄遷息州刺史，法令清靜，德化大行。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to inspector of Xizhou; laws and ordinances were clear and tranquil, and moral transformation was greatly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to inspector of Xizhou, where his laws were clear and tranquil and moral transformation flourished.

sentences.zh: 時屬平陳之役，征人在路，有疾病者，景茂撤減俸祿，為饘粥湯藥，分賑濟之，賴全活者以千數。

translations.literal: At the time it fell during the campaign to pacify Chen; conscripts were on the road, and those who fell ill—Jingmao drew from and reduced his salary and stipend to make gruel, porridge, soup, and medicine, distributing relief; those who relied on this to survive fully numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign to pacify Chen, conscripts on the march who fell ill were aided from Jingmao's salary: he provided gruel, soup, and medicine, saving thousands of lives.

sentences.zh: 上聞而嘉之，詔宣告天下。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and commended him, and ordered the announcement proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him and ordered his deed proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 十五年，上幸洛陽，景茂謁見，時年七十七。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the emperor visited Luoyang; Jingmao had an audience at age seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the emperor visited Luoyang; Jingmao had an audience at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 上命升殿坐，問其年幾。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to ascend the hall and be seated, and asked his age.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had him ascend the hall and take a seat, then asked his age.

sentences.zh: 景茂以實對。

translations.literal: Jingmao answered according to the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Jingmao answered truthfully.

sentences.zh: 上哀其老，嗟歎久之。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied his age and sighed long.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pitied his age and sighed at length.

sentences.zh: 景茂再拜曰：「呂望八十而遇文王，臣逾七十而逢陛下。」

translations.literal: Jingmao bowed twice and said: "Lü Wang at eighty met King Wen; your servant, past seventy, has encountered Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Jingmao bowed twice and said, "Lü Wang met King Wen at eighty; I, past seventy, have met Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 上甚悅，賜物三百段。

translations.literal: The emperor was very pleased and granted three hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and granted three hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「景茂修身潔己，耆宿不虧，作牧化人，聲績顯著。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Jingmao cultivates his person and purifies himself; in old age he is not diminished; as pastoral governor he transforms the people; his reputation and achievements are conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Jingmao has cultivated himself without decline in old age; as a pastoral governor he has transformed the people, and his reputation and achievements are outstanding.

sentences.zh: 年終考校，獨為稱首，宜升戎秩，兼進籓條。

translations.literal: In the year-end assessment he alone is foremost in praise; he should be advanced in military rank and concurrently promoted in territorial governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the year-end assessment he ranks first; he should be advanced in military rank and promoted in territorial office.

sentences.zh: 可上儀同三司，伊州刺史。」

translations.literal: He may be made Upper Commissioner with Equal Protocol to the Three Excellencies and inspector of Yizhou."
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed Upper Commissioner with Equal Protocol to the Three Excellencies and inspector of Yizhou."

sentences.zh: 明年，以疾征，吏人號泣於道。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned on account of illness; officials and people wailed along the road.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled because of illness; officials and commoners wept along the road.

sentences.zh: 及疾愈，復乞骸骨，又不許，轉道州刺史。

translations.literal: When his illness recovered, he again begged to return his bones; again it was not permitted, and he was transferred to inspector of Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he recovered, he again requested retirement, was again refused, and was transferred to inspector of Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 悉以秩俸買牛犢雞豬，散惠孤弱不自存者。

translations.literal: He entirely used his salary and stipend to buy calves, chickens, and pigs, distributing kindness to orphans and the weak who could not support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his entire salary buying calves, chickens, and pigs to distribute to orphans and the destitute who could not support themselves.

sentences.zh: 好單騎巡人，家至戶入，閱視百姓產業。

translations.literal: He liked to tour the people alone on horseback, entering every house and household, inspecting the common people's livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: He liked to tour alone on horseback, visiting every household to inspect the people's livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 有修理者，于都會時乃褒揚稱述。

translations.literal: Those who had improved their estates—at the time of the general assembly he would praise and proclaim them.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had improved their estates he praised publicly at the seasonal assembly.

sentences.zh: 如有過惡，隨即訓導，而不彰也。

translations.literal: If there were faults and wrongs, he would immediately instruct and guide them, but not expose them.
translations.idiomatic: If there were faults, he corrected them through private instruction rather than public exposure.

sentences.zh: 由是人行義讓，有無均通，男子相助耕耘，婦人相從紡績。

translations.literal: Thereupon people practiced righteousness and yielding; those with goods and those without shared equally; men helped one another in plowing, women followed one another in spinning.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the people practiced mutual courtesy and shared what they had; men helped one another in the fields and women worked together at the loom.

sentences.zh: 大村或數百戶，皆如一家之務。

translations.literal: Large villages might have several hundred households, all treating affairs as one family.
translations.idiomatic: In large villages of several hundred households, people conducted their affairs as one family.

sentences.zh: 其後請政事，上優詔聽之。

translations.literal: Later he requested to retire from government affairs; the emperor with a gracious edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Later he asked to retire from office, and the emperor graciously granted his request.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，上明公楊紀出使河北，見景茂神力不衰，還以狀奏。

translations.literal: During Renshou, Duke Shangming Yang Ji went on a mission to Hebei, saw that Jingmao's vigor had not declined, and on returning memorialized the fact.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era, Duke Shangming Yang Ji traveled to Hebei, found Jingmao still vigorous in old age, and reported this to the throne on his return.

sentences.zh: 於是就拜淄州刺史，賜以馬轝，便道之官。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed inspector of Zizhou on the spot, granted a carriage with horses, and went to office by the direct route.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed inspector of Zizhou, granted a carriage, and sent directly to his post.

sentences.zh: 前後曆職，皆有德政，論者稱為良牧。

translations.literal: In successive offices before and after, he all had virtuous administration; commentators called him a good pastoral governor.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he held, his administration was benevolent, and commentators hailed him as an exemplary pastoral governor.

sentences.zh: 大業初卒官，年八十七。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye he died in office at age eighty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daye era he died in office at the age of eighty-seven.

sentences.zh: 諡曰康。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 身死之日，諸州人吏赴喪者數千人，或不及葬，皆望墳慟哭，野祭而去。

translations.literal: On the day of his death, officials and people from the various prefectures who came to the funeral numbered several thousand; some could not reach the burial, and all gazed toward the tomb and wept bitterly, performing wild sacrifices and departing.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he died, thousands of officials and commoners from many prefectures came to mourn; those who could not reach the burial wept toward his tomb and departed after offering sacrifices in the open countryside.

sentences.zh: 辛公義，隴西狄道人也。

translations.literal: Xin Gongyi, a man of Didao in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Gongyi was a native of Didao in Longxi commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖徽，魏徐州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hui was regional inspector of Xuzhou in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hui had served the Wei as regional inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 父季慶，青州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Jiqing was inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiqing had been inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 公義早孤，為母氏所養，親授書傳。

translations.literal: Gongyi was orphaned early, raised by his mother, who personally taught him the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, Gongyi was raised by his mother, who personally taught him the classics.

sentences.zh: 周天和中，選良家子任太學生，以勤苦著稱。

translations.literal: During Zhou's Tianhe and Zhonghe eras, he was selected as a son of a good family to serve as an Imperial Academy student and became known for diligence and hardship.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhou Tianhe and Zhonghe eras he was selected as an Imperial Academy student from a respectable family and became known for his tireless diligence.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，召入露門學，令受道義。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wu he was summoned into the Dew Gate Academy and ordered to receive the Way and its principles.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu he was summoned to the Dew Gate Academy to study moral doctrine.

sentences.zh: 每月集御前令與大儒講論，數被嗟異，時輩慕之。

translations.literal: Each month he was gathered before the emperor to discourse with great Confucians; he was repeatedly sighed over in wonder, and contemporaries admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Each month he debated the classics before the emperor with eminent scholars, repeatedly won the emperor's admiration, and was envied by his peers.

sentences.zh: 建德初，授宣納中士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiande he was appointed Herald, Middle Rank.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jiande era he was appointed Herald of the middle rank.

sentences.zh: 從平齊，累遷掌治上士、掃寇將軍。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Qi and was repeatedly promoted to Director of Governance, Upper Rank, and Sweeping the Barbarians General.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaign to pacify Qi and rose through several posts to Director of Governance, Upper Rank, and Sweeping the Barbarians General.

sentences.zh: 高祖作相，授內史上士，參掌機要，

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu served as Chancellor, he was appointed Palace Scribe, Upper Rank, and participated in grasping confidential matters.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu served as chancellor, Gongyi was appointed Palace Scribe of the upper rank and took part in confidential state affairs.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年，除主客侍郎，攝內史舍人事，賜爵安陽縣男，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang, he was appointed Vice Minister of Guests, acted in the affairs of Palace Scribe Attendant, and was granted the title Baron of Anyang county with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaihuang, he was appointed Vice Minister of Guests, acted as Palace Scribe Attendant, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Anyang with a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 每陳使來朝，常奉詔接宴。

translations.literal: Whenever envoys from Chen came to court, he regularly received edicts to receive and entertain them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever envoys from Chen came to court, he was regularly ordered to receive and entertain them.

sentences.zh: 轉駕部侍郎，使往江陵安輯邊境。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of the Transport Bureau and sent to Jiangling to pacify and settle the borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of the Transport Bureau and sent to Jiangling to pacify the borderlands.

sentences.zh: 七年，使勾檢諸馬牧，所獲十餘萬匹。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was sent to inspect all horse pastures; more than one hundred thousand head were recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was sent to inspect the horse pastures and recovered more than one hundred thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 高祖喜曰：「唯我公義，奉國罄心。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said with pleasure: "Only my Gongyi exhausts his heart in serving the state."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said with delight, "Only my Gongyi serves the state with his whole heart."

sentences.zh: 從軍平陳，以功除岷州刺史。

translations.literal: He followed the army in pacifying Chen and for merit was appointed inspector of Minzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the army in the conquest of Chen and, for his merit, was appointed inspector of Minzhou.

sentences.zh: 土俗畏病，若一人有疾，即闔家避之，父子夫妻不相看養，孝義道絕，由是病者多死。

translations.literal: The local custom feared illness; if one person fell ill, the whole household avoided him; father and son, husband and wife did not care for one another; the ways of filial piety and righteousness were cut off—hence many of the sick died.
translations.idiomatic: The local custom feared disease: when one person fell ill, the entire household fled; fathers, sons, husbands, and wives refused to care for one another, and filial duty was abandoned—so many of the sick died.

sentences.zh: 公義患之，欲變其俗。

translations.literal: Gongyi was distressed by this and wished to change the custom.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi was distressed by this and wished to change the custom.

sentences.zh: 因分遣官人巡檢部內，凡有疾病，皆以床輿來，安置廳事。

translations.literal: He therefore dispatched officials to patrol within his jurisdiction; all who were ill were brought on beds and litters and placed in the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched officials throughout his jurisdiction to bring every sick person on a litter to the main hall of his office.

sentences.zh: 暑月疫時，病人或至數百，廳廊悉滿。

translations.literal: In the hot months during epidemics, the sick sometimes reached several hundred, and the halls and corridors were all full.
translations.idiomatic: During summer epidemics the sick sometimes numbered in the hundreds, filling every hall and corridor.

sentences.zh: 公義親設一榻，獨坐其間，終日連夕，對之理事。

translations.literal: Gongyi personally set out one couch, sat alone among them all day and through the night, and conducted affairs facing them.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi set up a couch among them and sat there alone day and night, conducting official business in their midst.

sentences.zh: 所得秩俸，盡用市藥，為迎醫療之，躬勸其飲食，於是悉差，方召其親戚而諭之曰：「死生由命，不關相著。

translations.literal: His salary and stipend he entirely used to buy medicine, summoned physicians to treat them, and personally urged their food and drink; thereupon all recovered, and only then did he summon their kin and instruct them: "Life and death are by fate and have nothing to do with contact.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his entire salary on medicine and physicians, personally urged the patients to eat, and when all had recovered he summoned their families and said, "Life and death are ordained by fate and have nothing to do with contagion.

sentences.zh: 前汝棄之，所以死耳。

translations.literal: Before, you abandoned them—that is why they died.
translations.idiomatic: You abandoned them before—that is why they died.

sentences.zh: 今我聚病者，坐臥其間，若言相染，那得不死，病兒復差！

translations.literal: Now I gather the sick and sit and lie among them; if it were said that infection spreads, how could I not die—yet the sick children have recovered!
translations.idiomatic: Now I sit and sleep among the sick; if disease were contagious, how could I remain alive—yet the sick have all recovered!

sentences.zh: 汝等勿覆信之。」

translations.literal: You must not again believe this."
translations.idiomatic: Do not believe such nonsense again."

sentences.zh: 諸病家子孫慚謝而去。

translations.literal: The sons and grandsons of the sick families departed in shame and thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The families of the sick departed ashamed and grateful.

sentences.zh: 後人有遇病者，爭就使君，其家無親屬，因留養之。

translations.literal: Later when people fell ill they vied to go to the commissioner; if their families had no kin, he kept and nurtured them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the sick rushed to the commissioner; those without family he kept and cared for himself.

sentences.zh: 始相慈愛，此風遂革，合境之內呼為慈母。

translations.literal: They began to practice mutual kindness and love; this custom was thereby reformed, and within the whole territory he was called the Loving Mother.
translations.idiomatic: Mutual care took root, the old custom vanished, and throughout the prefecture he was called the Loving Mother.

sentences.zh: 後遷牟州刺史，下車，先至獄中，因露坐牢側，親自驗問。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to inspector of Mouzhou; on dismounting from his carriage he first went to the prison, and in the open air sat beside the prisoners, personally examining and questioning them.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as inspector of Mouzhou, he went straight to the prison on taking office, sat in the open air beside the prisoners, and personally examined each case.

sentences.zh: 十餘日間，決斷咸盡，方還大廳。

translations.literal: Within more than ten days all judgments were completed, and only then did he return to the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: Within a fortnight he had disposed of every case, and only then returned to the main hall.

sentences.zh: 受領新訟，皆不立文案，遣當直佐僚一人，側坐訊問。

translations.literal: When receiving new lawsuits he never set up documents; he sent one assistant on duty to sit at his side and conduct inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: For new lawsuits he kept no written records; he sent one assistant to sit beside him and conduct the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 事若不盡，應須禁者，公義即宿廳事，終不還閤。

translations.literal: If the matter was not finished and detention was required, Gongyi lodged in the main hall and never returned to his quarters.
translations.idiomatic: If a case required detention, Gongyi slept in the main hall and never returned to his private quarters.

sentences.zh: 人或諫之曰：「此事有程，使君何自苦也！」

translations.literal: Someone admonished him: "This matter has its schedule—why does the commissioner torment himself!"
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged him, "These matters have their proper schedule—why torment yourself so!"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「刺史無德可以導人，尚令百姓系于囹圄，豈有禁人在獄而心自安乎？」

translations.literal: He answered: "The inspector lacks virtue to guide the people, yet still keeps the common people bound in prison—how could one detain people in jail and feel at ease in heart?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "An inspector without virtue to guide his people still keeps them in prison—how can I detain people in jail and feel at ease?"

sentences.zh: 罪人聞之，咸自款服。

translations.literal: When the guilty heard this, all of themselves confessed and submitted.
