translations.idiomatic: When the prisoners heard this, they all confessed willingly.

sentences.zh: 後有欲諍訟者，其鄉閭父老遽相曉曰：「此蓋小事，何忍勤勞使君。」

translations.literal: Later when someone wished to contend in lawsuit, the village elders of his neighborhood hastily informed one another: "This is but a small matter—how can we bear to trouble the commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: When someone later wished to sue, the village elders would say to one another, "This is a trifling matter—how can we trouble the commissioner for it?"

sentences.zh: 訟者多兩讓而止。

translations.literal: Most litigants yielded to one another on both sides and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Most disputes ended with both parties yielding to each other.

sentences.zh: 時山東霖雨，自陳、汝至於滄海，皆苦水災。

translations.literal: At the time in the east there was continuous rain; from Chen and Ru to the eastern sea all suffered flood disaster.
translations.idiomatic: At that time heavy rains afflicted the east; from Chen and Ru to the coast all suffered flooding.

sentences.zh: 境內犬牙，獨無所損。

translations.literal: Within his territory the land was jagged like dog's teeth, yet alone it suffered no damage.
translations.idiomatic: Though his territory lay amid the flooded regions, it alone suffered no damage.

sentences.zh: 山出黃銀，獲之以獻。

translations.literal: The mountains produced yellow silver; he obtained it and presented it as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow silver was found in the mountains, and he presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔水部郎婁崱就公義禱焉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Lang of the Water Bureau Lou Ce to go to Gongyi and pray there.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Lou Ce of the Water Bureau to pray with Gongyi.

sentences.zh: 乃聞空中有金石絲竹之響，

translations.literal: Then in the empty air was heard the sound of metal, stone, silk, and bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: Then music of metal, stone, silk, and bamboo was heard in the air.

sentences.zh: 仁壽元年，追充揚州道黜陟大使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Renshou, he was subsequently appointed Promotion and Demotion Commissioner of the Yangzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Renshou, he was subsequently appointed Promotion and Demotion Commissioner of the Yangzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 豫章王暕恐其部內官僚犯法，未入州境，預令屬公義。

translations.literal: Prince of Yuzhang Jian feared that officials within his domain would violate the law; before entering the prefectural border he beforehand ordered them placed under Gongyi's jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian of Yuzhang, fearing that officials in his domain might break the law, ordered them placed under Gongyi's authority before Gongyi entered the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 公義答曰：「奉詔不敢有私。」

translations.literal: Gongyi answered: "In carrying out the edict I dare not show partiality."
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi replied, "In carrying out my commission I dare show no favoritism."

sentences.zh: 及至揚州，皆無所縱舍，暕銜之。

translations.literal: When he reached Yangzhou he spared none, and Jian harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Yangzhou he spared no offender, and Prince Jian bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 及煬帝即位，揚州長史王弘入為黃門侍郎，因言公義之短，竟去官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, Yangzhou Chief Clerk Wang Hong entered court as Attendant at the Yellow Gate and spoke of Gongyi's faults; in the end he left office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, Yangzhou chief clerk Wang Hong entered court as Attendant at the Yellow Gate, denounced Gongyi's faults, and Gongyi was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 吏人守闕訴冤，相繼不絕。

translations.literal: Officials and people guarded the palace gate to plead injustice, one after another without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners crowded the palace gate to plead his innocence without cease.

sentences.zh: 後數歲，帝悟，除內史侍郎。

translations.literal: Several years later the emperor understood and appointed him Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later the emperor realized his error and appointed him Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 未幾，起為司隸大夫，檢校右禦衛武賁郎將。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled as Grand Master of the Metropolitan Area and inspecting Brave Attendant General of the Right Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled as Metropolitan Censor and inspecting Brave Attendant General of the Right Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 從征至柳城郡卒，時年六十二。

translations.literal: He followed on campaign and died at Liucheng commandery at age sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He followed a campaign and died at Liucheng commandery at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 子融。

translations.literal: His son Rong.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Rong.

sentences.zh: 柳儉郭絢敬肅

translations.literal: Liu Jian, Guo Xuan, and Jing Su.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian, Guo Xuan, and Jing Su.

sentences.zh: 柳儉，字道約，河東解人也。

translations.literal: Liu Jian, styled Daoyue, was a man of Jie in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian, whose courtesy name was Daoyue, came from Jie in Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖元璋，魏司州大中正、相華二州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yuanzhang was Metropolitan Rectifier of Sizhou in Wei and regional inspector of Xiang and Hua.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yuanzhang had served the Wei as Metropolitan Rectifier of Sizhou and regional inspector of Xiang and Hua.

sentences.zh: 父裕，周聞喜令。

translations.literal: His father Yu was magistrate of Wenxi in Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu had been magistrate of Wenxi under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 儉有局量，立行清苦，為州裡所敬，雖至親昵，無敢狎侮。

translations.literal: Jian had breadth of capacity; his conduct was established in purity and hardship; he was respected by the district and neighborhood—even the most intimate dared not treat him lightly or insult him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian possessed breadth of character and lived in austere integrity; his neighbors respected him, and even close acquaintances dared not treat him familiarly.

sentences.zh: 周代曆宣納上士、畿伯大夫。

translations.literal: Under the Zhou he successively held Herald, Upper Rank, and Metropolitan Baron, Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he served as Herald of the upper rank and Metropolitan Baron, Grandee.

sentences.zh: 及高祖受禪，擢拜水部侍郎，封率道縣伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, he was promoted and appointed Vice Minister of the Water Bureau and enfeoffed as Earl of Shuaidao county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu founded the dynasty, Jian was promoted to Vice Minister of the Water Bureau and enfeoffed as Earl of Shuaidao.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出為廣漢太守，甚有能名。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as governor of Guanghan and had a very fine reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed governor of Guanghan and earned a strong reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 俄而郡廢。

translations.literal: Shortly the commandery was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery was soon abolished.

sentences.zh: 時高祖初有天下，勵精思政，妙簡良能，出為牧宰，以儉仁明著稱，擢拜蓬州刺史。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Gaozu had newly gained the realm, strove in spirit and pondered government, subtly selected the able and good to go out as pastoral governors; because Jian was renowned for benevolence and clarity, he was promoted and appointed inspector of Pengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu had just secured the realm and was selecting able administrators for the provinces, Jian's reputation for benevolent and enlightened rule won him appointment as inspector of Pengzhou.

sentences.zh: 獄訟者庭遣，不為文書，約束佐史，從容而已。

translations.literal: Those in prison or litigation he dismissed from the courtyard; he made no documents, merely restrained his assistants and clerks, and was at ease—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: He disposed of lawsuits in the courtyard without written records, relying on restrained assistants and his own calm judgment.

sentences.zh: 獄無系囚。

translations.literal: The prison had no detained prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: His prison held no long-term detainees.

sentences.zh: 蜀王秀時鎮益州，列上其事，遷邛州刺史。

translations.literal: Prince of Shu Xiu at the time garrisoned Yizhou; he listed and reported this matter upward, and Jian was transferred to inspector of Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiu of Shu, then stationed in Yizhou, reported his excellence to the throne, and Jian was transferred to inspector of Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 在職十餘年，萌夷悅服。

translations.literal: In office for more than ten years, the tribal peoples were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: During more than ten years in office, the tribal peoples were pleased and submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 蜀王秀之得罪也，儉坐與交通，免職。

translations.literal: When Prince of Shu Xiu was found guilty, Jian was implicated for communicating with him and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiu of Shu fell from favor, Jian was dismissed for having associated with him.

sentences.zh: 及還鄉里，乘敝車羸馬，妻子衣食不贍，見者咸嘆服焉。

translations.literal: When he returned to his home district he rode a worn cart and lean horses; his wife and children's food and clothing were insufficient; those who saw it all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Returning home in a worn cart with lean horses, his wife and children poorly clothed and fed, all who saw him admired his integrity.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，征之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, Jian was summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 于時以功臣任職，牧州領郡者，並帶戎資，唯儉起自良吏。

translations.literal: At the time those appointed for meritorious service, pastoral governors leading commanderies, all carried military credentials; only Jian rose from being a good official.
translations.idiomatic: At that time provincial governors appointed for military merit all held military credentials; only Jian had risen through civil administration.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其績，用特授朝散大夫，拜弘化太守，賜物一百段而遣之。

translations.literal: The emperor commended his achievements, specially granted him Grand Master of the Palace for Dispersing Affairs, appointed him governor of Honghua, granted one hundred bolts of goods, and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his record, specially granted him the title Grand Master for Dispersing Affairs, appointed him governor of Honghua, granted one hundred bolts of goods, and sent him to his post.

sentences.zh: 儉清節逾勵。

translations.literal: Jian's pure integrity was ever more encouraged.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's integrity grew ever stricter.

sentences.zh: 大業五年入朝，郡國畢集，帝謂納言蘇威、吏部尚書牛弘曰：「其中清名天下第一者為誰？」

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daye, on entering court, when all commanderies and states were gathered, the emperor said to Supervisor Su Wei and Minister of Personnel Niu Hong: "Among them, who has the purest reputation first under Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daye, when he came to court and all the prefectures were assembled, the emperor asked Supervisor Su Wei and Minister of Personnel Niu Hong, "Who among them has the finest reputation for integrity in the realm?"

sentences.zh: 威等以儉對。

translations.literal: Wei and the others answered with Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and the others named Jian.

sentences.zh: 帝又問其次，威以涿郡丞郭絢、潁川郡丞敬肅等二人對。

translations.literal: The emperor again asked who was next; Wei answered with the two men Assistant of Zhuo commandery Guo Xuan and Assistant of Yingchuan commandery Jing Su.
translations.idiomatic: Asked who ranked next, Wei named Guo Xuan, assistant of Zhuo commandery, and Jing Su, assistant of Yingchuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 帝賜儉帛二百匹，絢、肅各一百匹。

translations.literal: The emperor granted Jian two hundred bolts of silk, and Xuan and Su each one hundred bolts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted Jian two hundred bolts of silk and Xuan and Su each one hundred bolts.

sentences.zh: 令天下朝集使送至郡邸，以旌異焉。

translations.literal: He ordered envoys from throughout the realm attending court to escort them to their commandery lodges, thereby commending their distinction.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the envoys from throughout the realm to escort them home in honor of their distinction.

sentences.zh: 論者美之。

translations.literal: Commentators praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators praised the emperor's judgment.

sentences.zh: 及大業末，盜賊蜂起，數被攻逼。

translations.literal: Near the end of Daye, bandits rose like bees; he was repeatedly attacked and pressed.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daye era, rebels rose everywhere and repeatedly attacked his territory.

sentences.zh: 儉撫結人夷，卒無離叛，竟以保全。

translations.literal: Jian soothed and bound the people and tribes; in the end none deserted or rebelled, and he ultimately preserved the territory.
translations.idiomatic: Jian won over the people and tribes; none deserted him, and he preserved his territory to the end.

sentences.zh: 及義兵至長安，尊立恭帝，儉與留守李粲縞素于州，南向慟哭。

translations.literal: When the righteous army reached Chang'an and installed Emperor Gong, Jian with the garrison commander Li Can wore unhemmed white at the prefecture and wept bitterly facing south.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous armies reached Chang'an and installed Emperor Gong, Jian and garrison commander Li Can dressed in mourning at the prefectural seat and wept toward the south.

sentences.zh: 既而歸京師，相國賜儉物三百段，就拜上大將軍。

translations.literal: Shortly he returned to the capital; the Chancellor granted Jian three hundred bolts of goods and appointed him on the spot Grand General of the Upper Rank.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned to the capital; the chancellor granted him three hundred bolts of goods and appointed him Grand General of the Upper Rank on the spot.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，卒于家，時年八十九。

translations.literal: After more than a year he died at home at age eighty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he died at home at the age of eighty-nine.

sentences.zh: 郭絢，河東安邑人也。

translations.literal: Guo Xuan, a man of Anyi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xuan was a native of Anyi in Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 家素寒微。

translations.literal: His family had always been poor and humble.
translations.idiomatic: His family had always been poor.

sentences.zh: 初為尚書令史，後以軍功拜儀同，歷數州司馬長史，皆有能名。

translations.literal: At first he was a Secretariat Clerk; later for military merit he was appointed Commissioner with Equal Status, and successively served as Chief of Staff or Chief Clerk in several prefectures—all with a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a Secretariat clerk, later earned the rank of Commissioner with Equal Status through military merit, and served as chief of staff or chief clerk in several prefectures, earning a reputation for ability in each.

sentences.zh: 大業初，刑部尚書宇文弼巡省河北，引絢為副。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye, Minister of Punishments Yuwen Bi toured and inspected Hebei and brought Xuan as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daye era, Minister of Punishments Yuwen Bi toured Hebei and took Xuan as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 煬帝將有事於遼東，以涿郡為衝要，訪可任者。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang was about to undertake affairs in Liaodong; Zhuo commandery was a strategic point, and he sought someone fit for the post.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang planned the Liaodong campaign, Zhuo commandery was a strategic point, and he sought a capable administrator.

sentences.zh: 聞絢有幹局，拜涿郡丞，吏人悅服。

translations.literal: Hearing that Xuan had administrative capacity, he was appointed Assistant of Zhuo commandery; officials and people were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Xuan's administrative ability, the emperor appointed him assistant of Zhuo commandery, and officials and commoners alike were pleased.

sentences.zh: 數載，遷為通守，兼領留守。

translations.literal: After several years he was transferred to be Administrator and concurrently held the post of Garrison Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was promoted to administrator and concurrently served as garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 及山東盜賊起，絢逐捕之，多所克獲。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in the east, Xuan pursued and captured them, seizing many.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in the east, Xuan pursued them and captured many.

sentences.zh: 時諸郡無復完者，唯涿郡獨全。

translations.literal: At the time none of the commanderies remained intact; only Zhuo commandery alone was preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: While other commanderies fell apart, Zhuo alone remained intact.

sentences.zh: 後將兵擊竇建德於河間，戰死，人吏哭之，數月不息。

translations.literal: Later he led troops to attack Dou Jiande at Hejian, died in battle, and officials and people wept for him for months without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He later led troops against Dou Jiande at Hejian, was killed in battle, and officials and commoners mourned him for months without cease.

sentences.zh: 敬肅，字弘儉，河東蒲阪人也。

translations.literal: Jing Su, styled Hongjian, was a man of Puban in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Su, whose courtesy name was Hongjian, came from Puban in Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 少以貞介知名，釋褐州主簿。

translations.literal: In youth he was known for integrity and uprightness; he doffed commoner's dress as Prefecture Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Known from youth for his integrity, he received his first appointment as prefectural chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，為安陵令，有能名，擢拜秦州司馬，轉豳州長史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was magistrate of Anling, had a reputation for ability, was promoted and appointed Chief of Staff of Qinzhou, and transferred to Chief Clerk of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang era he served as magistrate of Anling, earned a reputation for ability, was promoted to chief of staff of Qinzhou, and transferred to chief clerk of Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，為衛州司馬，俱有異績。

translations.literal: During Renshou he was Chief of Staff of Weizhou; in both posts he had outstanding achievements.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era he served as chief of staff of Weizhou, achieving outstanding results in every post.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，遷潁川郡丞，

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he was transferred to Assistant of Yingchuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, he was transferred to assistant of Yingchuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 大業五年，朝東都，帝令司隸大夫薛道衡為天下群官之狀。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daye, he attended court at the Eastern Capital; the emperor ordered Metropolitan Censor Xue Daoheng to compose evaluations of officials throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daye, on attending court at the Eastern Capital, the emperor ordered Metropolitan Censor Xue Daoheng to evaluate officials throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 道衡狀稱肅曰：「心如鐵石，老而彌篤。」

translations.literal: Daoheng's evaluation of Su said: "His heart is like iron and stone; in old age he is ever more steadfast."
translations.idiomatic: Daoheng's evaluation read: "His heart is iron and stone; in old age he grows ever more steadfast."

sentences.zh: 時左翊衛大將軍宇文述當途用事，其邑在潁川，每有書屬肅。

translations.literal: At the time Left Guard General Yuwen Shu held power on the road; his home district was in Yingchuan, and he often sent letters entrusting matters to Su.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shu, the powerful Left Guard General whose home district lay in Yingchuan, often sent letters asking favors of Su.

sentences.zh: 肅未嘗開封，輒令使者持去。

translations.literal: Su never once broke the seal; he always ordered the messenger to take them away unopened.
translations.idiomatic: Su never opened them and always sent the messenger away with the letters unopened.

sentences.zh: 述賓客有放縱者，以法繩之，無所寬貸。

translations.literal: When Shu's guests were unrestrained, he bound them with the law and showed no lenience.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu's guests broke the law, he punished them without lenience.

sentences.zh: 由是述銜之。

translations.literal: Hence Shu harbored resentment against him.
translations.idiomatic: Shu therefore bore a grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 八年，朝於涿郡，帝以其年老有治名，將擢為太守者數矣，輒為述所毀，不行。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he attended court at Zhuo commandery; the emperor, because he was old and had a reputation for governance, several times was about to promote him to governor, but each time Shu slandered him and it did not go through.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when he attended court at Zhuo, the emperor several times meant to promote the aged and renowned Su to governor, but each time Shu blocked it.

sentences.zh: 大業末，乞骸骨，優詔許之。

translations.literal: Near the end of Daye he begged to return his bones; a gracious edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daye era he requested retirement, and a gracious edict granted it.

sentences.zh: 去官之日，家無餘財。

translations.literal: On the day he left office his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he left office his household had no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，終於家，時年八十。

translations.literal: After more than a year he died at home at age eighty.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he died at home at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 劉曠，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Liu Kuang—it is not known from where he came.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kuang's place of origin is unknown.

sentences.zh: 性謹厚，每以誠恕應物。

translations.literal: His nature was careful and generous; he always responded to things with sincerity and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Careful and generous by nature, he always met people with sincerity and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，為平鄉令，單騎之官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was magistrate of Pingxiang and went to office alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang era he became magistrate of Pingxiang and rode alone to take up his post.

sentences.zh: 人有諍訟者，輒丁甯曉以義理，不加繩劾，各自引咎而去。

translations.literal: When people had contentious lawsuits he would calmly instruct them in principle and reason, impose no punishment, and each would take blame upon himself and depart.
translations.idiomatic: When people came to sue one another, he calmly explained what was right, imposed no punishment, and sent each party away blaming himself.

sentences.zh: 所得俸祿，賑施窮乏。

translations.literal: His salary and stipend he used to relieve the poor and destitute.
translations.idiomatic: He used his salary to aid the poor.

sentences.zh: 百姓感其德化，更相篤勵，曰：「有君如此，何得為非！」

translations.literal: The common people were moved by his moral transformation and encouraged one another all the more, saying: "With a lord like this, how could we do wrong!"
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his moral influence, the people encouraged one another, saying, "With a magistrate like this, how could we do wrong!"

sentences.zh: 在職七年，風教大洽，獄中無系囚，爭訟絕息，囹圄盡皆生草，庭可張羅。

translations.literal: In seven years in office customs and teaching were greatly harmonized; the prison had no detained prisoners; contentious lawsuits ceased entirely; the jail grew grass throughout, and in the courtyard one could spread a net.
translations.idiomatic: During seven years in office moral teaching flourished; the prison held no detainees, lawsuits ceased, weeds grew in the jail yard, and birds could be netted in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 及去官，吏人無少長，號泣于路，將送數百里不絕。

translations.literal: When he left office, officials and people young and old wept along the road; those escorting him continued for several hundred li without cease.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office, officials and commoners of every age wept along the road and escorted him for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 遷為臨潁令，清名善政，為天下第一。

translations.literal: He was transferred to magistrate of Linying; his pure reputation and good administration were first under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to magistrate of Linying, he again ranked first in the realm for integrity and good government.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射高熲言其狀，上召之，及引見，勞之曰：「天下縣令固多矣，卿能獨異於眾，良足美也！」

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Gao Jiong reported his situation; the emperor summoned him, and when he was introduced and received audience, comforted him saying: "Magistrates throughout the realm are indeed many, yet you alone can differ from the multitude—truly worthy of praise!"
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Gao Jiong reported his excellence; the emperor summoned him and said at their meeting, "Magistrates are many throughout the realm, yet you alone stand apart—truly admirable!"

sentences.zh: 顧謂侍臣曰：「若不殊獎，何以為勸！」

translations.literal: He turned and said to attending ministers: "If we do not reward him exceptionally, how shall we encourage others!"
translations.idiomatic: Turning to his ministers, he said, "Without exceptional reward, how can we encourage others!"

sentences.zh: 於是下優詔，擢拜莒州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon a gracious edict was issued and he was promoted and appointed inspector of Juzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued a gracious edict promoting Kuang to inspector of Juzhou.

sentences.zh: 王伽，河間章武人也。

translations.literal: Wang Jia, a man of Zhangwu in Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jia was a native of Zhangwu in Hejian commandery.

sentences.zh: 開皇末，為齊州行參軍，初無足稱。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaihuang he was Acting Staff Officer of Qizhou; at first there was nothing worth mentioning.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaihuang era he served as acting staff officer of Qizhou, initially without distinction.

sentences.zh: 後被州使送流囚李參等七十餘人詣京師。

translations.literal: Later he was sent by the prefectural commissioner to escort more than seventy exiled prisoners including Li Can to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was later assigned to escort more than seventy exiled prisoners, including Li Can, to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時制，流人並枷鎖傳送。

translations.literal: The regulation of the time required that exiles all be transported in cangues and fetters.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations required that exiles be transported in cangues and fetters.

sentences.zh: 伽行次滎陽，哀其辛苦，悉呼而謂之曰：「卿輩既犯國刑，虧損名教，身嬰縲絏，此其職也。

translations.literal: When Jia stopped at Xingyang he pitied their hardship, called them all together and said: "You have violated the state's punishment and damaged reputation and teaching; your bodies bear fetters—this is your due.
translations.idiomatic: Stopping at Xingyang, Jia pitied their hardship and addressed them all: "You have violated the law and damaged moral teaching; wearing fetters is your due punishment.

sentences.zh: 今復重勞援卒，民獨不愧於心哉！」

translations.literal: Yet now you again heavily burden the escort soldiers—should the people not feel ashamed in heart!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet you also burden the escort soldiers—should the people not feel ashamed?"

sentences.zh: 參等辭謝。

translations.literal: Can and the others declined and thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Can and the others thanked him.

sentences.zh: 伽曰：「汝等雖犯憲法，枷鎖亦大辛苦。

translations.literal: Jia said: "Although you violated the statutes, the cangues and fetters are also great hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Jia said, "Though you broke the law, the cangues and fetters are cruel hardship.

sentences.zh: 吾欲與汝等脫去，行至京師總集，能不違期不？」

translations.literal: I wish to remove them for you; you will go to the capital and assemble there—can you not miss the deadline?"
translations.idiomatic: I wish to remove them; you will travel to the capital and assemble there on your own—can you keep the deadline?"

sentences.zh: 皆拜謝曰：「必不敢違。」

translations.literal: They all bowed and thanked him, saying: "We surely dare not violate it."
translations.idiomatic: They all bowed and promised, "We will not fail you."

sentences.zh: 伽於是悉脫其枷，停援卒，與期曰：「某日當至京師，如致前卻，吾當為汝受死。」

translations.literal: Jia thereupon removed all their cangues, dismissed the escort soldiers, and set a date with them: "On such-and-such a day you must reach the capital; if you cause delay or retreat, I shall die for you."
translations.idiomatic: Jia removed all their cangues, dismissed the escorts, and set a date: "You must reach the capital by then; if any of you flee, I will accept death in your place."

sentences.zh: 舍之而去。

translations.literal: He released them and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He released them and went on his way.

sentences.zh: 流人咸悅，依期而至，一無離叛。

translations.literal: The exiles were all pleased; they arrived on schedule, and not one deserted or rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The exiles were delighted; they all arrived on time without a single defection.

sentences.zh: 上聞而驚異之，召見與語，稱善久之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and was startled and struck by this; he summoned Jia for an audience and conversation and praised him at length.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this he was astonished, summoned Jia, and praised him at length.

sentences.zh: 於是悉召流人，並令攜負妻子俱入，賜宴於殿庭而赦之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned all the exiles, ordered them to bring their wives and children and enter together, granted a feast in the palace courtyard, and pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned all the exiles with their wives and children, feasted them in the palace courtyard, and pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔曰：「凡在有生，含靈稟性，咸知好惡，並識是非。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued: "All who possess life, endowed with spirit and nature, all know good and evil and likewise discern right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "All living beings endowed with spirit know good from evil and right from wrong.

sentences.zh: 若臨以至誠，明加勸導，則俗必從化，人皆遷善。

translations.literal: If faced with utmost sincerity and clearly guided and encouraged, then customs will surely follow transformation and all will move toward goodness.
translations.idiomatic: When met with utmost sincerity and clear guidance, customs will change and people will turn toward goodness.

sentences.zh: 往以海內亂離，德教廢絕，官人無慈愛之心，兆庶懷奸詐之意，所以獄訟不息，澆薄難治。

translations.literal: Formerly because within the seas there was disorder and separation, moral teaching was abandoned and cut off, officials had no hearts of kindness and love, and the multitude harbored crafty and deceitful intent—hence lawsuits never ceased and shallowness was hard to govern.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, when the realm was torn by chaos, moral teaching collapsed, officials lacked compassion, and the people turned crafty—hence lawsuits never ceased and society grew hard to govern.

sentences.zh: 朕受命上天，安養萬姓，思遵聖法，以德化人，朝夕孜孜，意在於此。

translations.literal: We received the mandate from Heaven, nurture and comfort the myriad clans, think to follow the sage's law and transform people through virtue—diligent morning and evening, Our intent lies in this.
translations.idiomatic: Having received Heaven's mandate, I seek to nurture my people, follow the sages' way, and transform them through virtue—this is my constant purpose.

sentences.zh: 而伽深識朕意，誠心宣導。

translations.literal: Yet Jia deeply understood Our intent and with sincere heart proclaimed and guided.
translations.idiomatic: Jia deeply understood my intent and taught them with sincere heart.

sentences.zh: 參等感悟，自赴憲司。

translations.literal: Can and the others were moved to awareness and of themselves went to the penal authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Li Can and the others were moved and presented themselves to the authorities of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 明是率土之人非為難教，良是官人不加曉示，致令陷罪，無由自新。

translations.literal: It is clear that the people throughout the land are not hard to teach; truly it is that officials do not enlighten and show them, causing them to fall into crime with no means to renew themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Clearly the people of the realm are not hard to teach; it is officials who fail to instruct them, driving them into crime with no path to reform.

sentences.zh: 若使官盡王伽之儔，人皆李參之輩，刑厝不用，其何遠哉！」

translations.literal: If officials were all of Wang Jia's kind and the people all of Li Can's sort, punishments could be set aside unused—how far off would that be!"
translations.idiomatic: If all officials were like Wang Jia and all people like Li Can, punishments could be set aside—how far off is that day!"

sentences.zh: 於是擢伽為雍令，政有能名。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jia was promoted to magistrate of Yong and had a reputation for able administration.
translations.idiomatic: Jia was then promoted to magistrate of Yong, where he earned a reputation for competent governance.

sentences.zh: 魏德深，本巨鹿人也。

translations.literal: Wei Deshen was originally a man of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Deshen was originally from Julu.

sentences.zh: 祖沖，仕周為刑部大夫、建州刺史，因家弘農。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chong served Zhou as Grand Master of Punishments and regional inspector of Jianzhou; the family then settled in Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chong had served the Zhou as Grand Master of Punishments and regional inspector of Jianzhou, after which the family settled in Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 父毗，郁林令。

translations.literal: His father Pi was magistrate of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pi had been magistrate of Yulin.

sentences.zh: 德深初為文帝挽郎，後曆馮翊書佐、武陽司戶書佐，以能遷貴鄉長。

translations.literal: Deshen at first was a mourning attendant for Emperor Wen; later he successively served as Clerk of Fengyi, Clerk of the Household Registry of Wuyang, and for ability was transferred to magistrate of Guixiang.
translations.idiomatic: Deshen began as a mourning attendant for Emperor Wen, later served as clerk in Fengyi and Wuyang, and was promoted to magistrate of Guixiang for his ability.

sentences.zh: 為政清淨，不嚴而治。

translations.literal: His administration was pure and tranquil; without severity he achieved order.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was pure and tranquil; he governed effectively without harshness.

sentences.zh: 會與遼東之役，徵稅百端，使人往來，責成郡縣。

translations.literal: It happened to coincide with the Liaodong campaign; levies and taxes multiplied in every way, envoys came and went, and responsibility was pressed upon commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign, levies multiplied and envoys constantly pressed the commanderies and counties for fulfillment.

sentences.zh: 于時王綱弛紊，吏多贓賄，所在征斂，下不堪命。

translations.literal: At the time the royal regulations were lax and disordered; officials mostly took bribes; wherever one looked there was collection and extraction, and subordinates could not bear the commands.
translations.idiomatic: Discipline had collapsed, officials took bribes everywhere, and the people could not bear the exactions.

sentences.zh: 唯德深一縣，有無相通，不竭其力，所求皆給，百姓不擾，稱為大治。

translations.literal: Only in Deshen's one county did those with goods and those without share with one another; he did not exhaust their strength, and whatever was sought was supplied; the common people were not disturbed, and it was called greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Only in Deshen's county did people share what they had, strength was not exhausted, every demand was met without disturbing the people, and the county was called a model of good order.

sentences.zh: 于時盜賊群起，武陽諸城多被淪陷，唯貴鄉獨全。

translations.literal: At the time bandits rose in groups; many cities of Wuyang were overrun and lost, only Guixiang alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose everywhere, most cities in Wuyang fell, but Guixiang alone remained intact.

sentences.zh: 郡丞元寶藏受詔逐捕盜賊，每戰不利，則器械必盡，輒徵發於人，動以軍法從事，如此者數矣。

translations.literal: Assistant of the commandery Yuan Baocang received an edict to pursue and capture bandits; whenever battle went badly weapons were always exhausted, and he would immediately levy and draft from the people, often applying military law—this happened several times.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Yuan Baocang was ordered to pursue bandits; whenever battles went badly and weapons were exhausted, he drafted the populace under military law—this happened repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 其鄰城營造，皆聚於廳事，吏人遞相督責，晝夜喧囂，猶不能濟。

translations.literal: In neighboring cities all construction was gathered in the main hall; officials and clerks supervised and blamed one another in turn; day and night there was clamor, yet they still could not finish in time.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring cities crowded all construction work into the government hall, with officials supervising one another day and night in noisy haste, yet still could not finish on time.

sentences.zh: 德深各問其所欲任，隨便修營，官府寂然，恆若無事。

translations.literal: Deshen asked each what task he wished to undertake, let them build and repair as convenient; the government offices were silent, always as if nothing were happening.
translations.idiomatic: Deshen asked each worker what task he preferred and let them proceed at will; his offices remained quiet, as if nothing were amiss.

sentences.zh: 唯約束長吏，所修不須過勝餘縣，使百姓勞苦。

translations.literal: He only restrained the senior clerks that what was built need not exceed the other counties and cause the common people hardship.
translations.idiomatic: He only required that the work not exceed what other counties demanded, lest the people suffer undue hardship.

sentences.zh: 然在下各自竭心，常為諸縣之最。

translations.literal: Yet those below each exhausted their hearts on their own, and his county was constantly foremost among the counties.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his subordinates gave their full effort, and his county consistently ranked first.

sentences.zh: 尋轉館陶長，貴鄉吏人聞之，相與言及其事，皆歔欷流涕，語不成聲。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to magistrate of Guantao; when the officials and people of Guixiang heard, they spoke together of the matter, all sobbing and shedding tears that their words could not form sound.
translations.idiomatic: Soon transferred to magistrate of Guantao, the officials and people of Guixiang wept together at the news, unable to speak through their tears.

sentences.zh: 及將赴任，傾城送之，號泣之聲，道路不絕。

translations.literal: When he was about to take up his post, the whole city saw him off; the sound of wailing never ceased along the road.
translations.idiomatic: When he departed for his new post, the whole city saw him off, and the sound of weeping never ceased along the road.

sentences.zh: 既至館陶，闔境老幼皆如見其父母。

translations.literal: When he reached Guantao, old and young throughout the territory were as if seeing their own parents.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Guantao, old and young throughout the territory received him as they would their own parents.

sentences.zh: 有猾人員外郎趙君實，與郡丞元寶藏深相交結，前後令長未有不受其指麾者。

translations.literal: There was a cunning man, Outer Office Attendant Zhao Junshi, who was deeply connected with Assistant Yuan Baocang; successive magistrates and chiefs had none who did not accept their direction.
translations.idiomatic: A cunning Outer Office Attendant named Zhao Junshi was deeply allied with Assistant Yuan Baocang; no previous magistrate had refused their orders.

sentences.zh: 自德深至縣，君實屏處於室，未嘗輒敢出門。

translations.literal: From the time Deshen arrived in the county, Junshi kept himself secluded in his room and never dared rashly to go out the door.
translations.idiomatic: From the day Deshen arrived, Junshi secluded himself indoors and dared not venture out.

sentences.zh: 逃竄之徒，歸來如市。

translations.literal: Those who had fled and scattered returned like filling a market.
translations.idiomatic: Fugitives returned in crowds.

sentences.zh: 貴鄉父老冒涉艱險，詣闕請留德深，有詔許之。

translations.literal: The elders of Guixiang braved hardship and danger, went to the palace gate to request that Deshen be kept, and an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The elders of Guixiang braved hardship to petition the throne to retain Deshen, and an edict granted their request.

sentences.zh: 館陶父老復詣郡相訟，以貴鄉文書為詐。

translations.literal: The elders of Guantao again went to the commandery to sue one another, claiming the Guixiang documents were fraudulent.
translations.idiomatic: The elders of Guantao then sued at the commandery, claiming the Guixiang documents were fraudulent.

sentences.zh: 郡不能決。

translations.literal: The commandery could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery could not decide the matter.

sentences.zh: 會持節使者韋霽、杜整等至，兩縣詣使訟之，乃斷從貴鄉。

translations.literal: When commissioners with credentials Wei Ji, Du Zheng, and others arrived, both counties went to the commissioners to litigate, and the decision followed Guixiang.
translations.idiomatic: When commissioners Wei Ji and Du Zheng arrived, both counties appealed to them, and the decision favored Guixiang.

sentences.zh: 貴鄉吏人歌呼滿道，互相稱慶。

translations.literal: The officials and people of Guixiang sang and shouted filling the roads, congratulating one another.
translations.idiomatic: The officials and people of Guixiang celebrated in the streets.

sentences.zh: 館陶眾庶合境悲哭，因而居住者數百家。

translations.literal: The multitude of Guantao throughout the territory wept bitterly; because of this several hundred households came to reside there.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Guantao wept throughout the territory, and several hundred households moved to Guixiang to live under him.

sentences.zh: 寶藏深害其能。

translations.literal: Baocang deeply resented his ability.
translations.idiomatic: Baocang deeply resented his ability.

sentences.zh: 會越王侗徵兵于郡，寶藏遂令德深率兵千人赴東都。

translations.literal: When Prince of Yue Tong levied troops in the commandery, Baocang then ordered Deshen to lead one thousand troops to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Tong of Yue levied troops in the commandery, Baocang ordered Deshen to lead one thousand men to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 俄而寶藏以武陽歸李密。

translations.literal: Shortly Baocang surrendered Wuyang to Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Baocang surrendered Wuyang to Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 德深所領，皆武陽人也，以本土從賊，念其親戚，輒出都門東向慟哭而反。

translations.literal: Those Deshen led were all men of Wuyang; because their homeland followed the rebel, thinking of their kin they would go out the capital gate, face east, weep bitterly, and return.
translations.idiomatic: Deshen's troops were all from Wuyang; when their homeland joined the rebels, they went to the capital gate, faced east, wept for their kin, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 人或謂之曰：「李密兵馬近在金墉，去此二十餘裡。

translations.literal: Someone said to them: "Li Mi's troops and horses are near at Jinyong, a little more than twenty li from here.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to them, "Li Mi's army is at Jinyong, only twenty-odd li away.

sentences.zh: 汝必欲歸，誰能相禁，何為自苦如此！」

translations.literal: If you insist on returning, who can forbid you—why torment yourselves like this!"
translations.idiomatic: If you insist on returning, who can stop you—why torment yourselves so!"

sentences.zh: 其人皆垂泣曰：「我與魏明府同來，不忍棄去，豈以道路艱難乎！」

translations.literal: Those men all wept and said: "We came together with Magistrate Wei of the Bright Hall; we cannot bear to abandon him—is it because the road is hard!"
translations.idiomatic: They all wept and said, "We came with Magistrate Wei; we cannot abandon him—not because the road is hard!"

sentences.zh: 其得人心如此。

translations.literal: Such was how he won people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the devotion he inspired.

sentences.zh: 後與賊戰，沒於陣，貴鄉、館陶人庶至今懷之。

translations.literal: Later he fought with the rebels and perished in battle; the people of Guixiang and Guantao to this day cherish his memory.
translations.idiomatic: He later fought the rebels and died in battle; the people of Guixiang and Guantao cherish his memory to this day.

sentences.zh: 時有櫟陽令渤海高世衡、蕭令彭城劉高、城皋令弘農劉熾，俱有恩惠。

translations.literal: At the time there were the magistrate of Liyang Gao Shiheng of Bohai, the magistrate of Xiao Liu Gao of Pengcheng, and the magistrate of Chenggao Liu Chi of Hongnong—all had kindness and favor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the magistrates Gao Shiheng of Liyang in Bohai, Liu Gao of Xiao in Pengcheng, and Liu Chi of Chenggao in Hongnong were all noted for their kindness.

sentences.zh: 大業之末，長吏多贓汙，衡、高及熾清節逾厲，風教大洽，獄無系囚，為吏人所稱。

translations.literal: Near the end of Daye many chief officials were corrupt; Shiheng, Gao, and Chi had pure integrity ever more strict, customs and teaching greatly harmonized, prisons had no detained prisoners, and they were praised by officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daye era, when many officials were corrupt, Shiheng, Gao, and Chi maintained ever stricter integrity; moral teaching flourished, their prisons held no detainees, and officials and commoners alike praised them.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：古語云，善為水者，引之使平，善化人者，撫之使靜。

translations.literal: The historian says: An old saying runs, "Those skilled with water lead it to make it level; those skilled at transforming people soothe them to make them tranquil."
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: An old saying holds that those skilled with water guide it until it runs level, and those skilled at transforming people soothe them until they grow calm.

sentences.zh: 水準則無損於堤防，人靜則不犯于憲章。

translations.literal: When water is level the dikes and embankments suffer no harm; when people are tranquil they do not violate regulations and statutes.
translations.idiomatic: When water runs level, the dikes are unharmed; when people are tranquil, they do not violate the law.

sentences.zh: 然則易俗移風，服教從義，不資於明察，必藉於循良者也。

translations.literal: Thus to change customs and shift winds, to accept teaching and follow righteousness, does not rely on keen scrutiny—it must borrow upright and good officials.
translations.idiomatic: Thus to change customs and shift public morals, to make people accept teaching and follow righteousness, does not depend on harsh scrutiny but on upright officials.

sentences.zh: 彥光等皆內懷直道，至誠待物，故得所居而化，所去見思。

translations.literal: Yanguang and the others all inwardly cherished the straight Way and treated things with utmost sincerity; therefore where they resided they transformed, and when they departed they were missed and remembered.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang and the others all cherished integrity within and treated people with utmost sincerity; where they served they transformed society, and when they left they were missed.

sentences.zh: 至於景茂之遏惡揚善，公義之撫視疾病，劉曠之化行所部，德深之愛結人心，雖信臣、杜詩、鄭渾、硃邑，不能繼也。

translations.literal: As for Jingmao's checking evil and promoting good, Gongyi's comforting and tending the sick, Liu Kuang's transformation practiced in his jurisdiction, Deshen's love binding people's hearts—even Xin Chen, Du Shi, Zheng Hun, and Zhu Yi could not continue such deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Jingmao's restraint of evil and promotion of good, Gongyi's care for the sick, Liu Kuang's moral transformation of his district, and Deshen's winning of people's hearts—even Xin Chen, Du Shi, Zheng Hun, and Zhu Yi could scarcely have matched them.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「愷悌君子，人之父母。」

translations.literal: The Odes says: "The gentle and easy noble is the people's father and mother."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes says, "The gentle noble is the people's father and mother."

sentences.zh: 豈徒言哉！

translations.literal: Is it mere words!
translations.idiomatic: This is no empty phrase!

sentences.zh: 恭懿所在尤異，屢簡帝心，追既往之一眚，遂流亡于道路，惜乎！

translations.literal: Where Gongyi was was especially exceptional; he repeatedly won the emperor's regard—yet pursuing one past fault, he was driven to wander on the roads. Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi's service was especially distinguished and repeatedly won the emperor's regard, yet for one past fault he was driven into exile on the roads—a pity!

sentences.zh: 柳儉去官，妻子不贍，趙軌秩滿，酌水餞離，清矣！

translations.literal: When Liu Jian left office his wife and children had insufficient support; when Zhao Gui's term ended they offered water as a farewell gift—how pure!
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jian left office his family lacked means to live; when Zhao Gui's term ended the people offered him only water as a farewell gift—how pure indeed!
